faqs.answer: Be present for the first session and for the last five minutes of the others. The diagnostic session produces observations worth hearing face to face, and the end-of-session handover is where you learn what was covered, what the homework is and whether the plan has changed. For Year 9 and 10 students a parent in the flat but not in the room usually works best. For a Year 11 candidate sitting in on the lesson tends to be counterproductive, because the student performs for you instead of thinking. Protect the handover and skip the rest.

faqs.question: How do we arrange society gate access for a weekly tutor visit?
faqs.answer: Set it up once, before the first lesson, instead of at the gate every week. Most buildings in Kandivali East will convert a visitor pass into a standing weekly entry if a resident gives the security desk the tutor's name, mobile number and the fixed day and time. Societies inside Thakur Complex handle this routinely because the township is accustomed to regular service visitors. Send your wing and flat number plus the nearest landmark to the tutor the day before the first session. Ten minutes lost at a gate is a sixth of the lesson gone.

faqs.question: When should we start if the exam series is in the spring?
faqs.answer: Before the winter mocks, and ideally in Year 10. A tutor who starts in Year 10 can build method; one who starts after the mock results come home is triaging, and triage has a lower ceiling. The practical constraint on this corridor is availability rather than ability: the fortnight after Thakur Complex families read their mock results is the busiest enquiry period of the year, and the tutors with strong Extended science records are the first to be fully booked. Starting in September gives you choice; starting in January gives you whoever is left.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Maths, Physics and Chemistry together?
faqs.answer: Occasionally at Core level, rarely well at Extended. The honest position is that Mathematics and Physics overlap enough for one capable tutor to hold both, because the algebra and graph work transfer. Chemistry is a different discipline and a tutor claiming all three at Extended is usually selling availability. For a Year 11 student with two problem subjects, two specialists on two evenings beats one generalist for two hours. For a Year 9 student the calculation is different and one strong all-round science tutor can be the right and cheaper choice.

faqs.question: What happens to a session we miss because of a school event?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule in week one, not after the first clash. Mumbai IGCSE school calendars generate predictable collisions: sports week, the annual concert, pre-board timetables that shift without much notice. The arrangement most families here settle on is that notice before the previous day moves the session, notice on the day forfeits it, and a short online substitute is offered when the obstacle is travel rather than time. Writing that down at the start prevents the slow resentment that ends more tutoring relationships on this corridor than bad teaching ever does.

sections.heading: From enquiry to an IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West gets matched on three facts and one constraint. The facts are the examining board, the year group, and the subject code or at least the exact subject title as the school writes it. The constraint is the evening window your household can actually protect for the next two terms. Give us those four things and the shortlist is usually accurate first time. Leave the board out and we are guessing between two syllabuses that set different papers, mark different skills and publish different command-word lists.

The board matters more than parents expect. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both run IGCSE courses, both are common across Mumbai, and schools around Kandivali West use either depending on the campus and sometimes the subject. A tutor who has spent six years on Cambridge papers can read an Edexcel paper perfectly well, but will not instinctively know how its questions are phrased or how its mark schemes reward working. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from a paper, that instinct is the whole purchase.

The shortlist that comes back is two or three profiles, each stating which board, which subjects and which years that tutor is teaching this term. Not "experienced in IGCSE". Teaching, this term, Year 10 Cambridge Chemistry, for example. Then a free discovery call, fifteen minutes, directly with the tutor. Ask what they would look at in session one with your child and you will know within a minute whether they teach the syllabus or recite it.

Teaching starts after you say yes and not before. From there it is a written review every two to four weeks naming topics covered, topics now secure and topics still weak, and there is no term contract to escape from. Families in Kandivali West commonly pause through the examination break in the spring and restart in June, and nothing about our arrangement penalises that.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: which IGCSE is your child sitting?
paragraphs: Check the top of a past paper your child has brought home, or ask the subject teacher, before you book anybody. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel are separate examination boards running separate IGCSE qualifications, and the difference is not cosmetic. Paper structures differ, the way extended-response questions are phrased differs, and the mark schemes reward different amounts of visible working. A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Maths candidate and a Cambridge IGCSE Maths candidate are both doing quadratics, and are not practising the same exam.

Within Cambridge, several subjects are entered at either Core or Extended tier, and that decision sets a ceiling on what the student can be awarded. Within Pearson Edexcel, some subjects have Foundation and Higher papers that work similarly. Either way, the tier or paper your child is entered for determines which questions they will even see, and it is decided by the school on the evidence of a year of marked work. We will not override that from the outside, and nor should a tutor you are paying by the hour.

What a good tutor does instead is make the decision visible. Put two questions from the same topic side by side, one from each tier, ask the student to attempt both cold, and the gap stops being theoretical. Parents around Kandivali West who do this in Year 9 rather than Year 11 have a real choice; those who leave it until the entry deadline are taking the school's view on trust, which is often right but is no longer their decision.

For paper structures, component names, coursework options and whether a subject has a practical or an alternative-to-practical route, read the current syllabus document for the year your child sits the examination, or ask the school's examinations officer. Boards revise these on their own schedule and old handouts circulate for years. Any IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents are considering should be able to tell you where to find that document rather than quote you a half-remembered structure.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to staff in Kandivali West?
paragraphs: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, Business and English are well covered, and a shortlist for any of them usually comes back inside a day or two. The harder asks are second languages, Computer Science with real coursework support, Accounting, and Art and Design where the portfolio needs someone who has actually marked one. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Kandivali West can be found for, that scarcity list is the honest constraint, and the register behind all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Kandivali West is deeper in the sciences than in the arts, and it is the reason we sometimes come back and say the strongest candidate is available online rather than in your living room.

The subject-level work in Years 9 to 11 divides into three jobs. First, the content that was taught while the student was coasting, usually a block from early Year 9 that everything since has been built on. Second, the technique: reading a command word correctly, showing the working a mark scheme pays for, and answering the question asked rather than the one revised. Third, the coursework or practical component where one exists, which is marked work sitting inside the final result and is routinely treated as homework by students who do not realise what it counts for.

The command-word problem is the one that moves marks fastest. A Year 10 student who writes a beautiful description when the question said "explain" loses marks on content they knew perfectly. The same student answering "compare" with two separate paragraphs and no comparison loses them again. This is not a knowledge gap and no amount of re-teaching the topic will fix it. It takes a tutor sitting beside the student with a marked paper, going through it line by line, saying what the examiner was paying for and what it was not.

Practical and coursework components need calendar planning rather than cramming. A science student who leaves a practical write-up until the week it is due produces something that cannot be improved; one who drafts it three weeks early gets feedback and a second attempt. The same applies to an extended piece in a language or a business case study. We tell tutors to schedule those backwards from the school's internal deadlines in the first week, because retrofitting them in January is how good students end up with ordinary results.

sections.heading: Home classes, online or both for IGCSE in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home classes come first for this age group for a straightforward reason: a Year 9 or Year 10 student is usually still learning how to work, not just what to learn. A tutor in the room sees the pen stop, sees the guess, sees the student skip the working and jump to an answer. All three are invisible on a video call. For a student who cannot yet sit with a problem for ten minutes without reaching for a phone, home tuition across this part of Mumbai is the format that works, and the only one we would start with.

Online earns its place in two specific cases. The first is scarcity: if your child is sitting a second language or an unusual option, the best-qualified teacher may be nowhere near Link Road, and an IGCSE online tutor in Kandivali West is a better answer than a nearby generalist reading the syllabus a week ahead of the student. The second is a disciplined Year 11 candidate in the final stretch who wants two extra paper-marking sessions a week and cannot fit two more travelling slots into the schedule. Online is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who cannot yet work alone, and we will say so rather than take the booking.

Hybrid is where most families here end up by the second term. One travelling session for teaching that needs a shared page and a watched pen, one online session for marking past papers and running a short pre-test clinic. It takes the travel cost out of half the week, it survives a monsoon evening when Link Road has stopped moving, and it gives a student a second contact point without adding an hour of commute to anyone's day.

Group tuition is the option we are most often asked about and least often recommend here. Two students at the same board, the same year and genuinely the same level can work well, and siblings sometimes do. Three students at different tiers in one room means the tutor teaches to the middle and nobody gets the diagnosis they are paying for. A shared room is also not the same purchase as an IGCSE private tutor in Kandivali West working one to one with your child. If cost is the constraint, a shorter weekly session with the right specialist beats a longer one shared with strangers.

sections.heading: How do we verify an IGCSE tutor before you meet them?
paragraphs: Four checks, every time, before a profile reaches a parent. A government photograph identity document on file. A degree in the subject rather than a general teaching certificate. A stated history of which board and which years they have taught, because IGCSE Physics and Diploma Programme Physics are different jobs and so are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel. And references from families who have actually been taught by them, obtained by us, not testimonials the tutor supplied. Every IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West on our register has cleared those four.

We are equally clear about what we do not check. We run no police record verification and claim none. We cannot audit any tutor's account of how a student's result changed, because results statements belong to candidates and no platform in Mumbai can see them. If a service tells you it has verified a tutor's grade record, it is describing something it cannot do. What we can tell you is precisely how long this person has taught your child's board at your child's year group, and what the families before you said.

The checks that matter most are yours, and they take four minutes on the discovery call. Ask which board and year they are teaching right now. Ask them to describe the last piece of coursework or practical write-up they gave feedback on, and what the feedback was. Ask what they would do in session one with your child. Then ask how they handle a student who has not done the work set. The answers to those four separate the specialist from the graduate who tutors on the side, and no profile can do it for you.

Two warning signs are worth naming. A tutor who promises a specific grade before meeting the student is telling you they do not understand what they are selling. A tutor who wants payment for a block of twenty sessions before teaching one is managing their own risk with your money. Pay per session or in small blocks, keep the right to stop, and the rest of the relationship stays honest.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and what the tier decision costs later
paragraphs: The tier decision is the single most consequential thing that happens to a Cambridge IGCSE student, and it happens quietly. Several subjects are entered at Core or at Extended, the award ranges differ, and the entry is made by the school in Year 10 or Year 11 on the evidence of the student's marked work. Nobody sits the family down to explain it. Parents around Kandivali West usually discover it exists when the entry form comes home, by which point the evidence the decision rests on is already a year old.

What it costs later is access. An award from the lower tier can close a door at a school that requires a specific grade for a subject at the next stage, and students who later want a science or mathematics pathway in the Diploma Programme or at A Level sometimes find the tier they were entered for in Year 11 shapes what they can start in Year 12. This is not a reason to push every child up a tier. It is a reason to know the deadline, know what the school is looking for, and get the evidence in before it, which is a tutoring job with a hard date on it.

The practical sequence is this. In Year 9 or early Year 10, ask the subject teacher directly what tier the student is currently tracking towards and what would need to change to move. Get that answer in writing if you can. Then set a tutor on precisely those topics with a target of showing improvement on school assessments before the entry window, not after. A student who moves tier on genuine evidence is better prepared than one argued up by a parent, and the second usually unravels in the paper.

This is also where IGCSE tuition fees in Kandivali West become easier to think about, because the question stops being a rate and becomes a budget with a deadline. Fees move with the board, the year group, the scarcity of the subject, the distance the tutor travels and the length and frequency of sessions. A tutor who lives on Link Road costs a family less than one crossing from the highway side in the evening peak, which is why we shortlist locally first. A focused eight-week block before an entry decision is a different purchase from two years of weekly support, and knowing which one you are buying is more useful than any published price.

sections.heading: What four weeks of IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai should show
paragraphs: At four weeks, ignore marks and look at behaviour. Can the student start an unfamiliar question without being told how to begin? Can they say what the command word is asking before they write? Is homework arriving finished rather than half-attempted? Does the tutor's written review name topics, or does it praise effort? Those four answers tell you whether the match is working. Marks at four weeks tell you almost nothing, because a single assessment in that window may test a topic the tutor has not reached.

At one term, the diagnosis should be sharp even if the numbers are mixed. Both the tutor and you should be able to name the two or three weaknesses that remain and say what is being done about each one. For a Year 10 student the honest version often sounds like: algebraic manipulation is now secure, graph interpretation is improving, and extended-response questions still lose marks because the student writes too little. That is a working relationship. "She is doing much better" after twelve sessions is not, and it is grounds to ask harder questions.

Over a full examination cycle, timing decides how much is possible. A student who starts in June of Year 10 has time to rebuild the foundation under the current topic, and that is where the largest changes happen. A student who starts in January of Year 11 is doing technique, paper strategy and error reduction, which is genuinely valuable and is not foundation repair. Both are worth buying. They are different products, and a tutor who implies otherwise in February is selling rather than teaching.

When a match is not working, ending it is dull by design. Send us one sentence about what is wrong, the tutor finishes the session already in the diary, and you owe nothing further. We go back to the register with the brief corrected by what we learned, and a replacement shortlist for a common subject usually arrives within a few days. No notice period, no minimum term, no fee. If you would rather not say it to the tutor yourself, we will.

sections.heading: What to have ready before the first session in Kandivali West
paragraphs: Three things, and the second is the one families forget. The most recent report or progress sheet. One piece of the student's own marked work in the weak subject, ideally a test paper with the teacher's marks on it. And two evening windows that are genuinely free for the next two months, not aspirational ones. The marked paper is worth more than the report: it shows whether marks were lost on method, on misreading, on arithmetic or on running out of time, and those four problems need four different first sessions.

Session one is a diagnosis. Expect the tutor to watch more than they talk: a short check across recent topics, two questions attempted cold without help, a look at how the student takes notes and revises. Expect it to end with two or three named weaknesses and a plan for the next three sessions. Expect no lecture and no hour of homework on day one. If the first session was mostly explanation, raise it before the second rather than after the sixth.

Somebody should be in the flat and nobody should be in the room. A parent at the table changes how a fifteen-year-old answers a question they are unsure about, and a tutor cannot diagnose a student who is performing. Be around for the first ten minutes to hear the plan and the last five to hear the summary. The rest belongs to the two of them. If your society issues visitor passes from the flat rather than the gate, factor five minutes into the start time.

Parents who type best IGCSE tutor in Kandivali West into Google are asking a reasonable question with no honest ranking behind it. Judge a tutor on four things instead: the right board and year, a diagnosis you can follow after session one, written reviews that name topics, and a travel time that holds up on a Wednesday at 6.30pm. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents enquire about is not hard to find. One who clears those four for your child, your subject and your address is what a brief and a call are for.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child is on Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Look at the header of any past paper or specimen paper the school has sent home, or ask the subject teacher or examinations officer directly. The board is printed on every paper. It matters because an IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West who has taught Cambridge for years knows how Cambridge phrases questions and what its mark schemes pay for, and the equivalent is true for Pearson Edexcel. Both boards are common across Mumbai and some schools use different boards for different subjects, so check per subject rather than assuming the whole timetable is one board.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees depend on if you will not publish a price?
faqs.answer: Five things, and any honest range would be too wide to help you. Fees move with the examining board, the year group, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, and how long and how often sessions run. A Year 11 Extended-tier science specialist in the weeks before papers is scarcer than a Year 9 generalist. A tutor already on Link Road costs less than one crossing from the highway side at 6.30pm. faqs.question: Is it too late to start in January before papers in the spring?
faqs.answer: No, but be clear about what you are buying. A January start is technique work: reading command words properly, showing the working a mark scheme rewards, timing a paper, and cutting careless losses. It can move a result meaningfully. What it cannot do is rebuild a foundation gap from early Year 9, because there is no time. If a tutor tells you in January that a weak Year 11 student can be comprehensively fixed before the papers, they are selling. A June or September start buys the foundation work as well.

faqs.question: Will the tutor help with coursework and practical write-ups?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a boundary: a tutor teaches the skill and gives feedback on a draft, and does not write or dictate the work. Where an IGCSE subject carries coursework, a practical component or an alternative-to-practical route, those marks sit inside the final result and are routinely treated as ordinary homework by students. The useful tutor schedules them backwards from the school's internal deadline in the first week, so there is time for a draft, real feedback and a second attempt. Confirm the exact components with the school, because boards revise them.

faqs.question: Does somebody need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, and not in the room. A parent sitting at the table changes how a teenager answers something they are unsure of, which is precisely the behaviour the tutor needs to see. Be present for the first ten minutes while the tutor explains the plan, and the last five while they summarise what happened. Work from another room in between. If your building requires a visitor pass issued from the flat, tell us so the tutor builds five minutes into the arrival time.

faqs.question: My child says the subject teacher at school is the problem. Is a tutor the answer?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes it is the wrong first step. If a student is struggling in one subject while comfortable in the rest, the conversation with that subject teacher comes before hiring anyone, and a good tutor will say so on the discovery call. If marks have dropped across every subject at once, look at sleep, screens or something happening outside school before assuming a teaching problem. We would rather talk a parent out of a booking than take one that cannot work. A tutor fixes specific, named gaps.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 10 IGCSE student actually need?
faqs.answer: Most families here start with one ninety-minute session a week per subject and that is usually right. Two sessions a week makes sense in the final run-up to papers, or where a student has a genuine foundation gap and time to fix it. More than two in one subject is rarely about teaching and usually about supervision, which is cheaper to solve with a study routine than with a specialist. Start at one, read the first two written reviews, and increase only if the reviews name work that is not getting done.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IGCSE subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: For the sciences and for maths with physics, often yes, and it saves travel cost on an evening slot. For maths plus a language or a humanities subject, be cautious: a genuine specialist in both is rarer than a profile claiming both. Ask which of the two they are teaching to Year 11 this term and which they last taught two years ago. Where a tutor is strong in one and adequate in the other, we would rather send two profiles and let you decide than present one convenient match.

Those changes usually move marks, sometimes in the same cycle and sometimes in the next. A tutor who promises a specific grade before session one should be declined.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: which IGCSE pathway is your child on?
paragraphs: Check the syllabus code on your child's exercise book before you book anything. IGCSE is not one qualification but two parallel ones in Mumbai: Cambridge International Education runs its own subject syllabuses with their own four-digit codes, and Pearson Edexcel runs a separate International GCSE with its own specification numbers. Schools in the Central Suburbs use both, and some use one board for sciences and the other for English or a second language. A tutor who has taught only Cambridge Coordinated Sciences will know the content of an Edexcel paper but not its question style, its mark scheme vocabulary, or the way its practical assessment is handled. Parents booking IGCSE home tuition in Kanjurmarg should ask which board a tutor has actually taught to completion, not which board they have read about.

The second structural decision is tier. Several Cambridge subjects are offered at Core and Extended, and the entry is made by the school, usually in Year 10, sometimes provisionally in Year 9 and confirmed later. Core caps the grade available; Extended opens the full range but adds content and harder question types. Families often discover the entry has been made only when a report mentions it. If your child is capable of Extended but has been placed in Core because of one weak term, that is a conversation to have with the subject teacher early, and a reason to bring in a tutor before the entry is finalised rather than after. The reverse is also true: an Extended entry a child cannot carry produces a term of quiet demoralisation that no amount of home tutoring fixes comfortably.

Year group matters as much as board. Year 9 is foundation work where a tutor should be building habits and filling gaps from Years 7 and 8. Year 10 is where the assessed content accumulates and where coursework or practical components begin to appear in the school calendar. Year 11 is examination craft: timing, command words, showing method, and deciding which marks are realistically recoverable in the time left. The same subject specialist does not always suit all three. Across Mumbai the most common mismatch IB Gram sees is a strong Year 11 examination coach placed with a Year 9 student who needed patient foundation teaching instead.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects do Kanjurmarg families most often ask for?
paragraphs: Mathematics, the three sciences, English and a second language account for most requests in this part of Mumbai, and each fails in its own way. In Mathematics the recurring loss is not topic knowledge but presentation: a student who can reach the right answer mentally and writes down nothing earns a fraction of the marks on a structured question. In Physics and Chemistry the loss is usually the maths inside the science, rearranging a relationship under time pressure or handling units through a multi-step calculation. In Biology it is command words: describe, explain, suggest and compare ask for different things, and a student who answers all four the same way loses marks on content they know well. In English the loss is structure, not vocabulary.

An all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Kanjurmarg is rarely the right answer for a Year 11 student, and parents should be suspicious of anyone who offers it. One person can genuinely cover Mathematics and Physics, or Chemistry and Biology, or English and Economics. Beyond that the depth thins. Where a family needs three subjects at Extended tier, two tutors sharing the week is almost always better than one generalist carrying all three, and it costs less in wasted sessions than it appears to on paper. Where the child is in Year 9 and the problem is study habits rather than subject content, a single tutor across two or three subjects is reasonable and often preferable, because the habit work transfers.

Internal and coursework components deserve their own conversation. Depending on the board and subject, your child may face a practical assessment, a speaking component in a language, or school-managed coursework with internal deadlines that sit on top of the examination timetable. Do not take a weighting, duration or mark total from a tutor or from this page as fact: subject guides are revised on the boards' own cycles, so check the current specification or ask the school coordinator which components apply to your child's cohort. What a tutor should do is name the components your child faces, say which ones can still be improved at this point in the year, and say clearly which cannot.
bullets: Mathematics marks are lost on unshown method, not unknown topics
Science marks are lost on the maths inside the science
Command words separate describe, explain, suggest and compare answers

The practical effect is that Powai's tutor pool passes through Kanjurmarg daily, and families here can book from it without paying for the JVLR leg in travel time.

Distance is the wrong measure in the Central Suburbs. The right measure is whether the slot survives the evening peak. Within Kanjurmarg itself, a tutor arriving on foot from the station is not exposed to that risk at all. sections.heading: The school calendar Kanjurmarg parents actually plan around
paragraphs: Families in and around Kanjurmarg send children to Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai and NES International School, among others, and both run on an international calendar rather than the local board one. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service and is not affiliated with either school or with any school named on this page; they are listed because their calendars set the pressure points a tutor has to work around. The practical consequence is that the academic year's hard months are not the ones a parent raised on a March board examination expects. Assessment weeks, coursework deadlines and mock papers cluster differently, and a tutor who starts in the wrong month spends the first fortnight catching up rather than teaching.

The pattern most Central Suburbs families recognise looks roughly like this. The year opens in June with the monsoon, and the first six weeks are when a new topic is introduced fastest and gaps from the previous year are least visible. By late in the first term, school assessments begin to produce the report comment that sends a parent searching for an IGCSE home tutor in Kanjurmarg in the first place. The winter stretch carries mocks for Year 11 and the heaviest coursework load for Year 10. By the time the final examination series arrives, the realistic work is consolidation and timing, not new content. A tutor hired in that last window can still help, but what they can change is narrower and should be described honestly on the first call.

Two scheduling realities follow from that calendar. The first is that the best time to start home tuition is the term before the pressure, not during it, because a tutor who already knows the child can compress work in a crisis while a new one cannot. The second is that school holidays in a Mumbai international school rarely align with a tutor's other families, so a parent who wants continuity through Diwali or the winter break should say so when the slot is agreed rather than assume it. Families who sort both questions out in the first conversation lose far fewer weeks than those who treat the schedule as something to settle later.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix for IGCSE in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the right default for most IGCSE students in Mumbai, and the reason is supervision rather than quality of teaching. A tutor in the room sees the exercise book, sees what the child wrote before they corrected it, and sees the moment attention goes. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student who cannot yet work unsupervised for forty minutes, an IGCSE home tutor in Kanjurmarg will get more done in an hour than the same person online will get done in ninety minutes. Home classes also pull the parent into the loop without requiring a meeting: you hear the last five minutes of the lesson and you know what happened.

Online is genuinely better in three situations, and worth choosing deliberately in them. The first is subject scarcity: if your child needs a less commonly taught language or a specialist at the top of a subject, an IGCSE online tutor in Kanjurmarg drawn from elsewhere in Mumbai or beyond beats a nearby generalist. The second is examination season, when a short, frequent, screen-shared paper review is more useful than a long weekly visit and the travel time is better spent working. The third is a child who already studies independently and simply needs marking and direction. Online is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who cannot yet sit alone with a problem, and no amount of good software changes that.

The arrangement that works best across a full year for most families here is hybrid, and it is worth setting up on purpose rather than drifting into. One home visit a week carries the teaching and the accountability; one shorter online session mid-week handles the marking, the questions that came up in class, and the pre-assessment check. In practical terms this halves the exposure to the evening peak on JVLR and the Eastern Express Highway while keeping a person in the room weekly. When a family asks for IGCSE home tuition in Kanjurmarg and their child has three subjects to carry, hybrid is usually what the schedule can actually sustain from June through to the examination series.

sections.heading: How tutors are checked before they reach your gate in Mumbai
paragraphs: IB Gram verifies identity, qualifications and board-specific teaching history before a profile is shown to a parent, and the board history is the part that matters most. A tutor can hold a strong degree and still have never taken a class through a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel examination series, which is a different skill from knowing the subject. Verification therefore asks what the tutor has taught, to which board, at which tier, and for how long, and separates claimed experience from demonstrated experience. Where a tutor's history is in one board only, that is stated on the profile rather than smoothed over, because a parent choosing an IGCSE private tutor in Kanjurmarg deserves to know which specification the person actually lives in.

What the platform cannot do is judge the fit between a particular tutor and your particular child, and no screening process can. So there are four checks a parent should run themselves on the discovery call. Ask the tutor to describe how they would diagnose the problem in session one, and listen for whether the answer involves looking at your child's recent work. Ask which board and tier they have taught most recently. Ask what they will send you after four weeks and in what form. Ask what they will do if your child has not improved by then. A tutor who answers all four concretely is usually worth starting with, whatever their paper credentials.

There are warning signs that are worth acting on immediately. Be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success rate, or claims an affiliation with a named Mumbai school. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor does either, because the result depends on a child's work over months and on an examination they sit alone. Be equally wary of a tutor who will not do a short free call before being booked, who cannot say which board they teach, or who proposes a long prepaid package before a single lesson has happened. Those three together are the clearest signal that you are talking to a reseller rather than a teacher.

sections.heading: What do IGCSE home classes in Kanjurmarg actually cost?
paragraphs: IGCSE tuition fees in Kanjurmarg depend on five things, and no honest page can quote you a figure without knowing them. The first is board and tier: an Extended-tier Cambridge subject in Year 11 commands more than foundation work in Year 9, because the pool of people who can teach it well is smaller. The second is subject scarcity. Mathematics and the sciences have depth of supply in this corridor; a second language, Economics at the top end, or a specialist humanities subject has much less, and scarcity sets price more than anything else does. The third is session length and frequency, because two shorter sessions a week usually cost more in total than one long one and are often worth it.

The fourth factor is travel, and this is where Kanjurmarg is unusually well placed. A tutor who walks from Kanjurmarg station to your building is absorbing almost no travel cost, while the same tutor crossing JVLR to Powai in the evening peak is giving up another lesson's worth of time and will price accordingly. Families within walking distance of the station, or in the societies along the LBS Marg side, are effectively buying from the cheap end of the travel curve. The fifth factor is what you are actually asking for: ongoing weekly teaching, intensive pre-mock work, or coursework support near a deadline are three different jobs and are not priced the same.

The question parents should ask instead of the price question is the value question. Parents searching for the best IGCSE tutor in Kanjurmarg usually mean the tutor who will change the outcome most per rupee, and that is almost never the most expensive profile on the shortlist. It is the one whose subject and tier match exactly, who can hold the slot for thirty weeks without renegotiating it, and who sends you something concrete at four weeks. A cheaper tutor who cancels twice a month costs more than a dearer one who never does. Ask what happens to a missed session, whether the rate changes for examination-season intensity, and whether there is any lock-in, before the first lesson rather than in month three.

sections.heading: What four weeks of home tuition in Kanjurmarg should show
paragraphs: At four weeks you should be able to see three specific things, and a grade is not one of them. You should see a written diagnosis: which topics are weak, which are fine, and which marks were being lost to method rather than knowledge. You should see a change in how your child works, usually visible as method written out on problems they used to do in their head. And you should see at least one piece of marked work with the tutor's comments on it alongside the school's. If a tutor cannot produce those three at four weeks, the issue is not that progress is slow; it is that nobody is measuring anything, and that is the point to change tutor rather than wait.

Over a full term the realistic arc is narrower than most parents hope and broader than most fear. A student who was losing marks to presentation and timing often moves quickly, because the knowledge was already there and the fix is habit. A student with genuine content gaps from Years 7 and 8 moves more slowly, because the tutor is rebuilding foundations while the school keeps moving forward, and the first visible gain may be a term away. Over a full examination cycle, consistent weekly home tutoring plus the child's own work is a reasonable bet on improvement. It is not a promise, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades. Anyone who does is selling something other than teaching.

When a tutor is not working out, the useful thing is to say so early and specifically. Across Mumbai the most common reason a match fails is not competence but register: a tutor who teaches a Year 11 examination class brilliantly can lose a quiet Year 9 student completely. Tell IB Gram what is not working, in one or two sentences, and a replacement is shortlisted from the same pool without a renegotiation or a penalty. Four weeks in is the right moment for that conversation. Four months in, with a child who has quietly stopped doing the homework, is a much harder place to recover from, and it is the situation that most often ends with a family giving up on home tuition altogether.

sections.heading: Getting started with home tuition in Kanjurmarg, Mumbai
paragraphs: Have three things ready and the first call takes ten minutes. The first is the syllabus code or at least the board name from your child's exercise book, because that single detail removes half the guesswork from the shortlist. The second is the most recent school report or assessment paper, ideally the paper itself rather than the grade, since a tutor can read where marks went from the script and cannot read it from a number. The third is two or three weekly time slots that survive a normal week in Kanjurmarg, including the travel your child already does to school and back. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents ask about is less useful than a specialist who fits your actual week.

Session one should not look like teaching, and a parent who expects a lesson is sometimes disappointed by the right thing happening. A good first session is mostly diagnostic: the tutor works through recent questions with your child, watching where the method breaks, asking what the child was thinking rather than telling them the answer. By the end of it the tutor should be able to say which two or three things they will work on first and why, in language you can repeat to the school. If they instead start at page one of the textbook, they have not looked at your child's work, and that is worth raising before week two.

On the practical side, settle the building logistics the same week. Give the security desk at Runwal Greens or your own society the tutor's name and the standing slot so that the gate is not a weekly negotiation. Pick the room before the first lesson rather than during it. Decide whether a parent needs to be at home, which for a Year 9 student usually means yes at first and less so later. And agree what happens to a missed session on both sides. Families who settle those four questions in week one almost never lose a lesson to them, which over thirty weeks of IGCSE home tuition in Kanjurmarg is worth several sessions of teaching.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE home tutor start in Kanjurmarg?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days of the brief, and faster here than in most of the Central Suburbs. faqs.question: Does my child need a different tutor for Cambridge and Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Not a different person necessarily, but a tutor who has actually taught the board your school uses. Content overlaps heavily between Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel, but question style, command-word usage and mark scheme language do not, and marks live in that difference. Ask any tutor which board they have taken a class through to final papers most recently. If your school uses one board for sciences and another for English, say so in the brief, because it changes the shortlist. This is the single most common reason a competent tutor underperforms with a capable student.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE home tuition in Kanjurmarg cost per month?
faqs.answer: It depends on board and tier, subject scarcity, session length and frequency, and how far the tutor travels, so any figure quoted without those is guesswork. Mathematics and the sciences have good supply in this corridor and price accordingly; a less commonly taught language costs more because fewer people teach it. Kanjurmarg families within walking distance of the station pay less of a travel component than families deeper inside Powai. faqs.question: Can one tutor cover three IGCSE subjects at Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Rarely well, and a tutor who offers it without hesitation is worth questioning. One person can genuinely hold Mathematics and Physics, or Chemistry and Biology, or English and a humanities subject. Three Extended-tier subjects across different groups usually means depth is being traded for convenience, and the subject that suffers is the one your child is weakest in. Two tutors sharing the week costs less in wasted sessions than it looks like on paper. For a Year 9 student whose real problem is study habits rather than content, one tutor across two or three subjects is reasonable and often better.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring good enough for a Year 9 IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is the honest answer rather than the commercial one. A Year 9 student who cannot yet work alone with a hard problem for forty minutes needs someone in the room who can see the exercise book and catch the moment attention goes. Online suits a student who already studies independently, a scarce subject where the right specialist is elsewhere in Mumbai, and fast paper review during examination season. Many families here end up with one home visit a week plus a shorter online session mid-week, which is a better fit than either mode alone.

faqs.question: What should I expect after four weeks with no grade change?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis, visible change in how your child works, and at least one piece of marked work. Grades move on the school's assessment schedule, not on the tutor's, so four weeks is too early to read a report card. What is not too early is evidence that someone is measuring: which topics are weak, which marks were lost to method rather than knowledge, and what the tutor is working on first. If none of that exists at four weeks, change tutor rather than wait, because nothing is being tracked and another month will not fix that.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the lesson?
faqs.answer: For a Year 9 student, usually yes at first and less so once the pattern is set. The point is not supervision of the tutor but the handover: five minutes at the end where the tutor says what was covered and what the homework is saves a week of guessing. By Year 11, most students prefer the parent out of the room and the update by message instead, which works fine. What matters more is the room. A lesson in a living room with a television on competes with the house, and that loses more teaching time than an absent parent ever does.

Four months in, with a child who has quietly stopped doing the set work, is much harder to recover, and it is the point at which families give up on tutoring rather than on the tutor.

Powai is reached by road from Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar or Andheri East, and the JVLR evening peak is the real constraint on back-to-back slots there. sections.heading: Is your child sitting Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel?
paragraphs: Ask the school, because the answer changes the papers, the tiers and the past papers your tutor should be using. Most IGCSE schools in Thane and Mumbai follow Cambridge International Education, a smaller number follow Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a few run a mix across subjects. A tutor who has only taught one of the two will say so if you ask directly.

Cambridge runs many of its subjects in two tiers, Core and Extended, with different papers and a different range of grades available. Pearson Edexcel uses tiered entry in some subjects too, under its own names. The practical consequence is identical: a child entered at the lower tier cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and a child entered at the higher tier can lose heavily on questions pitched above them. Entry decisions are made by the school, usually in Year 10 or early Year 11, and they are the single most consequential academic decision of these two years.

Both boards publish a syllabus code for every subject, and it is the most useful thing a parent can carry into a tutoring conversation. A request for help with Physics is vague. A request for help with the Cambridge Physics syllabus your school entered the child for is specific, and it tells the tutor which paper set, which practical route and which command words to work from. Get the codes off the school's subject list or the exam entry sheet rather than guessing from a textbook cover.

Do not take component structures, paper counts or weightings from a blog, including this one. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel revise syllabuses on their own cycles, and a structure that was right for the cohort two years above your child may not be right for theirs. The current syllabus document for the exact year of entry is the only reliable source, and your school's examinations officer has it.
bullets: Ask the school which board each subject is entered under
Core or Extended entry caps or opens the grade range available
Carry the syllabus code into every tutoring conversation
Entry tiers are usually fixed in Year 10 or early Year 11
Check the syllabus for the year of entry, not an older one

sections.heading: Option blocks, entry codes and the subjects that go wrong in Year 10
paragraphs: Across Kasarvadavali enquiries the subjects that go wrong in Year 10 are predictable: Extended Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry once the mole calculations start, Economics and Business where evaluation marks appear for the first time, and a second language chosen because it looked easy in Year 8. Parents who ask about all IB and IGCSE subjects want one tutor in Kasarvadavali to carry everything, and it almost never ends well.

Option blocks are the constraint nobody mentions. Subjects are grouped, one choice per block, so the combination a child wants is sometimes not available and the school will not say that until the form comes back. If your child is aiming at engineering or medicine later, as many Mumbai families here are, check before the form closes that the block structure allows the science and mathematics combination those routes expect. A tutor can help you read the blocks, and a diagnostic session in the marginal subject is worth more than another conversation about aptitude.

Coursework and practical routes differ by subject and by school. Some subjects run a coursework component the school marks and the board moderates, others offer a written alternative paper in place of a practical examination, and the school decides which route it enters. This matters for tutoring because a coursework subject needs help with planning, drafting and the assessment criteria months before the exam, while an alternative-paper subject needs practice at reading somebody else's experiment off a page. Ask the subject teacher which route your child is on before you book anything.

Enquiries for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Kasarvadavali parents send in the days after a report usually name four subjects. Two of them are the real problem and two are collateral: a child who has lost confidence in Mathematics often stops trying in Physics as well. Fixing the first frequently fixes the second, which is why we push back on a four-subject request before agreeing to it.
bullets: Extended Mathematics and Physics dominate Year 10 enquiries here
Option blocks can block a science and mathematics combination
Ask which subjects run coursework and which run an alternative paper
Coursework subjects need help months before the written papers
Four-subject requests usually reduce to two real problems

sections.heading: Ghodbunder Road, Manpada and Balkum: who can actually reach Kasarvadavali
paragraphs: Look at it from the tutor's side of the windscreen. A tutor who lives in Manpada can teach a child in Kasarvadavali at 5pm and another in Balkum at 7pm, and still be home for dinner. A tutor who lives near Thane station can do one of those, and only if nothing goes wrong on Ghodbunder Road. Thane runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch is the piece that sets everyone's timetable.

The numbers behind that are plain. Twenty minutes off-peak from near the station, close to an hour in the evening. Mulund tutors do cross over, and some are very good, but a Mulund base plus the Eastern Express Highway plus the Ghodbunder leg is three variables on a Tuesday evening in July. Thane tutors cover Thane, and for a standing weekly commitment at the far west end that is the pool worth drawing from.

Year 11 is the exception that changes everything, and it is worth planning for. Once study leave starts, sessions move into the daytime, the Ghodbunder Road peak stops mattering, and a tutor from the station side or from Mulund becomes entirely workable for the six to eight weeks before the written papers. Several families here run a west Thane tutor through Years 9 and 10 and then add a specialist from further out for the final run, which is a sensible use of the geography rather than a compromise.

The transport that exists and the transport that does not both matter. Thane station carries the Central Line towards Kalyan and the Trans-Harbour Line towards Vashi, neither of which comes anywhere near here, and Ghodbunder Road itself is SH-42, carrying through traffic as well as local cars. An IGCSE home tutor in Kasarvadavali therefore arrives by road, every time, and in Mumbai that means the arrival time is a range rather than a time. Build fifteen minutes of slack into the slot and nobody starts the session apologising.
bullets: A Manpada base allows two sessions a night on this road
Twenty minutes off-peak from Thane station, near an hour at 6pm
Mulund tutors cross over, best suited to weekends and study leave
Study leave moves Year 11 sessions into the daytime
Ghodbunder Road is SH-42 and carries through traffic too

sections.heading: What should I ask my school before the Year 9 option form closes?
paragraphs: Four questions, in writing if possible: which board each subject is entered under, how the option blocks are grouped, when tier entry decisions are made, and which subjects carry coursework. Schools answer all four readily when asked by email, and the answers decide what kind of IGCSE home tuition is useful for the next two years.

Families on this stretch of Ghodbunder Road mostly send their children to Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, to NES International School, or to one of the international schools further into Mumbai. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not affiliated with any of these schools, and naming them here is local context rather than any kind of endorsement in either direction.

The school calendar, not the examination board calendar, is what creates the crunch weeks. Internal coursework deadlines, the mock timetable and the predicted-grade exercise are all set by the school, and in most IGCSE schools in Mumbai they cluster in two windows: late in the first term, and the January to February stretch when mocks run and predicted grades are finalised for applications. Those two windows are when the phone rings here.

Predicted grades deserve a paragraph of their own, because parents underestimate them. They are produced by the subject teachers from the evidence in front of them, usually the mock performance and the coursework to date, and they travel on to the schools and colleges your child applies to. A tutor cannot change a predicted grade. What tutoring before the mocks can change is the evidence the teacher has to work from, which is a reason to start in September rather than in February.
bullets: Ask in writing which board each subject is entered under
Ask how the option blocks are grouped before the form closes
Ask when tier entry decisions are taken and by whom
Mock season and predicted grades both land January to February
Tutoring changes the evidence, not the predicted grade itself

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or both for an IGCSE student in Kasarvadavali?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default for Years 9 and 10, for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching quality. A fifteen-year-old with a laptop and an open browser is a fifteen-year-old with a browser, and the main thing a tutor in the room provides at that age is the inability to drift. IGCSE home classes in Kasarvadavali also give the tutor access to the exercise book, the marked mock and the textbook the school actually uses, all of which say more than the child will.

An IGCSE online tutor in Kasarvadavali earns its place in three situations. A scarce subject is the first: Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics, Computer Science or a less common second language may have no specialist within reach on Ghodbunder Road, and a screen beats nobody. The second is Year 11 study leave, where short daily contact matters more than long weekly contact. The third is the fortnight before papers, when a twenty-minute call to go through one question is more valuable than a cancelled hour.

Hybrid is where most Year 10 families here end up, and it is not a fudge. One long session at the table each week, plus a mid-week upload of a past-paper attempt that the tutor marks and returns with comments, does more than two visits, because the marking is the teaching. The honest limit is that it only works if the child attempts the paper unsupervised. A child who needs someone sitting next to them to start is not ready for the upload half, and the arrangement should stay fully in person until they are.

The trade-off nobody mentions is the parent's time. Home tuition in Mumbai means a household that has to be quiet at a fixed hour, someone at the gate, and a room given over. Online costs none of that, which is precisely why some families overuse it. Be honest about which constraint you are actually solving, because a mode chosen for the household rather than the child shows up in the marks within a term.
bullets: Home tuition first for Years 9 and 10, where drift is the problem
Online for scarce Edexcel subjects with no local specialist
Online daily contact beats weekly contact during study leave
Hybrid works only if the child attempts papers unsupervised
Marking an uploaded past paper is teaching, not admin

sections.heading: How IGCSE tutors in Mumbai are checked, and what you should check
paragraphs: IB Gram verifies four things before a profile reaches you: identity, the qualification claimed, documented experience with the specific board and syllabus, and a subject conversation with someone who knows the papers. The third is where most applicants fall away. Teaching Physics for twenty years in another system is not the same as having taken a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel cohort through to a written series in Mumbai.

Then do your own checks, because fit is not verifiable from a document. Ask a shortlisted IGCSE home tutor in Kasarvadavali which board and tier they taught most recently, how they mark a past paper, and what they would do if there were no visible change after four weeks. Ask for a current family's number. The answer about marking is the revealing one: a tutor who marks to the published mark scheme and shows the child where the method marks went is doing the job.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a success rate, and be equally wary of one who will not say what they do not teach. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and the useful thing an experienced tutor gives you instead is a realistic range and the specific change that would move it. A parent searching for the best IGCSE tutor in Kasarvadavali is asking a question with no answer. The one with an answer is which tutor has taught this board, this tier and this subject recently.

Two checks that cost you nothing. Look at a marked past paper after a fortnight and see whether the corrections are in the child's handwriting or the tutor's. And ask your child, after session three, to explain one thing they learned without looking at a book. An IGCSE private tutor Kasarvadavali families keep through two years is one who has made the child the person doing the work.
bullets: Identity, qualification, board-specific experience and a subject conversation
Ask which board and tier the tutor taught most recently
Ask how they mark a past paper against the mark scheme
Corrections should be in the child's handwriting, not the tutor's
Ask your child to explain one thing without the book

sections.heading: The two-year clock: Year 9 to the May series in Mumbai
paragraphs: IGCSE is a two-year course that most families treat as a one-year course, and the cost of that is paid in Year 11. Year 9 sets the tiers and the option blocks. Year 10 builds the content and the coursework. Year 11 is almost entirely about papers, timing and the mechanics of answering, and there is no room in it to rebuild Year 9 algebra. The most useful month to start, in the Mumbai school year, is September of Year 10, and the most common month to start is January of Year 11.

Here is what the late start looks like in practice on Ghodbunder Road. A Year 11 student gets mock results in late January showing a fail in Extended Mathematics. The family finds a tutor in the first week of February. There are perhaps ten weeks to the written papers, two of which are lost to school revision programmes and one to a family commitment. Seven weeks at one session a week is seven hours. Seven hours cannot rebuild two years of algebra, and any tutor who says it can is taking your money. What seven hours can genuinely do is secure the method marks on the questions the student can nearly do, and that is worth real grades.

The far-west position of Kasarvadavali adds a twist here that does not apply in central Thane. Because peak-hour Ghodbunder Road puts the station side nearly an hour away, the weekday evening pool is small, and in February every family in west Thane is competing for it at once. The families who get the slot they want are the ones who booked in September. The ones who call in February take a Saturday morning, a daytime study-leave slot, or an online specialist. All three work. None of them is the slot they wanted.

IGCSE tuition fees in Kasarvadavali move on five things and travel is one of them, which is why the same tutor costs differently here and in Majiwada. The board and tier, the scarcity of the subject specialist, the session length, the number of sessions a month and the distance covered all feed in. Nobody should quote you a rate without asking the subject and the year group first. Ask for the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, and ask what happens to it during study leave, when sessions typically go up.
bullets: Year 9 sets tiers, Year 10 builds content, Year 11 is papers
September of Year 10 is the useful start, January of Year 11 the common one
Seven weeks secures method marks, not two years of algebra
February demand in west Thane exceeds the weekday evening supply
Fees move with board, tier, scarcity, session length and travel

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one exam series: what should change
paragraphs: At four weeks the measurable change is not in grades, it is in the exercise book. Working should be set out in steps, errors should be corrected in the child's own hand, and the child should be able to name the topic they are weakest on. If the book after a month looks like a set of copied notes, the tutor is lecturing and you should say so.

At one term, look at a timed past paper. The three things that should have moved are completion, method marks and the quality of the attempt on the last question. A student who used to leave the final two questions blank and now writes a partial method has gained real marks, even if the total has barely shifted. Ask the tutor to show you the marked script against the published mark scheme rather than reporting a percentage, because the percentage hides whether the gain is in the easy marks or the hard ones.

At one exam series, be honest about the ceiling. A child entered at Core cannot reach a grade the tier does not offer, however good the tutoring, and nobody should let you discover that in August. A child entered at Extended who started two years behind will usually land some distance below their classmates and still a long way above where they began. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not publish a success rate, because the number would tell you nothing about your own child.

If none of this is happening, the conversation belongs in week three. The four causes we see are the same every time: the tutor is pitched wrong for the tier, the slot is too late in the evening for this particular child, three subjects are being crammed into one hour, or the two of them simply do not get on. Three of those four are fixed without changing tutor. The fourth is a replacement, arranged from the west Thane pool, with the previous tutor's notes handed over so nobody starts again from zero.
bullets: Four weeks: steps in the working, corrections in the child's hand
One term: completion, method marks and the last-question attempt
Ask to see the marked script, not a reported percentage
Core entry caps the grade however good the tutoring is
Week three is when to raise a bad match, not week twelve

sections.heading: Booking IGCSE home tuition in Kasarvadavali: the first fortnight
paragraphs: Collect four documents before the first call and the whole thing moves faster: the subject list with board names, the most recent report, the marked mock paper if there is one, and the school's coursework deadline sheet for the term. The marked mock is the single most useful item. A tutor reads a script in ten minutes and learns more than a parent can convey in an hour.

Prepare the room rather than the child. A table that is not the dining table, two chairs facing across rather than side by side, a door that closes, and the phone in another room. For Years 9 and 10, be in the flat for the first few sessions. By Year 11 your presence is usually counterproductive, and the better arrangement is a three-minute summary from the tutor at the end.

Expect week one to be diagnosis and week two to feel like the real start. The first session should produce a written note: the topics that are secure, the topics that are not, and what the next four weeks will cover. If no note arrives, ask for one before the second session. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents recommend to each other is almost always one who writes things down.

Then fix the slot and defend it. For a student in Years 9 or 10 on Ghodbunder Road, pick the evening that will still be free in three months, tell the tutor the exam weeks and the school trips in advance, and agree now what happens to a session missed for traffic or illness. An IGCSE home tutor in Kasarvadavali who has the term's calendar plans around it; one who finds out on the night cancels.
bullets: Bring the subject list with board names and the marked mock
A table that is not the dining table, door closable, phone away
Expect a written note of secure and insecure topics after session one
Agree in advance what happens to a session missed for traffic
Pick the evening that will still be free in three months

faqs.question: Can a tutor commute to Kasarvadavali during Year 11 study leave?
faqs.answer: Yes, and study leave is the one period when the geography stops mattering. Sessions move into the daytime, Ghodbunder Road is clear, and a tutor from the Thane station side or from Mulund can reach Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes. Several families use a west Thane tutor through Years 9 and 10 and then bring in a subject specialist from further out for the six to eight weeks before the written papers. Book that second tutor in December rather than in March, because the same specialists are in demand across Thane and Mumbai at exactly the same time.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Kasarvadavali depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and travel is the local one. The board and the tier affect it, because an Extended specialist with recent Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel experience is scarcer than a Year 9 generalist. Subject scarcity affects it, session length affects it, and the number of sessions a month affects it. Then distance: a tutor driving the length of Ghodbunder Road twice a week is pricing that time whether or not the invoice itemises it. Ask for the monthly commitment rather than an hourly rate, and ask specifically what changes during study leave, when most families increase frequency.

faqs.question: Which evening slots work on Ghodbunder Road for a Year 10 student?
faqs.answer: The realistic weekday window here is 6.30pm to 8.30pm, and the earlier half of it is better. A Year 10 student bussed back from a Thane school is not usefully awake at 8.45pm, and a tutor arriving at 7.30 after the Ghodbunder Road crawl has already lost the best part of the session. Saturday or Sunday morning is the strongest slot available to families at this end of the road, and it is the only one long enough for a full timed paper. Many Year 10 families in this part of Mumbai run one long weekend session and one short weekday one.

faqs.question: Do you need the syllabus code before matching a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not to start, but it changes the match. The code tells us which board, which route and which paper set, and it separates tutors who have taught that exact syllabus from tutors who have taught the subject. You will find it on the school's subject list or the exam entry sheet. If you cannot find it, tell us the school and the year group and we will narrow it from there, then confirm with you before the first session. Starting without it is common. Finishing a term without it means somebody has been using the wrong past papers.

faqs.question: Should my child take Core or Extended Mathematics?
faqs.answer: The school decides the entry, but your view carries weight if you raise it early. Extended covers more and opens the higher grades, while Core is a shorter syllabus with a lower ceiling. The honest test is whether the child can currently work through an unfamiliar multi-step problem alone, not whether they are capable in principle. A child pushed to Extended who cannot will lose marks across the whole paper rather than only on the hard questions. One or two diagnostic sessions in Year 9 answer this better than any conversation, and the time to have it is before the tier is submitted.

faqs.question: We only found out at the mocks. Is February too late?
faqs.answer: It is late, not useless, and the honest answer depends on the subject. Ten weeks at one session a week is about ten hours, which cannot rebuild two years of foundations but can reliably secure the marks on questions the student nearly gets right already. In practice that means exam technique, method marks, timing and the two or three topics that appear on every paper. Expect the tutor to triage rather than teach the course. Any tutor who promises to cover the whole syllabus in February is either not reading the script or not telling you the truth.

faqs.question: Is a society gate pass needed for a weekly tutor visit?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and setting it up once saves ten minutes every week. Residential complexes along Ghodbunder Road run visitor registers or an app, and most will add a recurring weekly visitor if the resident requests it with the name, the day and the time. Do that before the first session rather than after. Send the tutor the tower and wing name too, because several of the newer clusters at this end have multiple towers behind one entrance and a wrong turn eats the start of the hour. Guards change shift, and a standing entry survives that where a phone call does not.

faqs.question: How many subjects should one tutor take for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Two is the sensible maximum, and one is often better in Year 11. A tutor who teaches Mathematics and Physics credibly is common, because the overlap is real. One who offers Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics is covering ground rather than teaching it. Where a child needs help in three subjects, two tutors is the better structure, with the weakest subject getting the longer slot and the clearer plan. The coordination cost is real and worth paying. A single tutor stretched across four subjects produces an hour that touches everything and changes nothing.

faqs.question: Does an online IGCSE tutor work as well as home tuition for a Year 9?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and this is the candid answer parents do not want. Online is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who cannot yet sit down and start without being asked, which describes most of them. What online does well is a scarce subject with no local specialist, short daily contact during study leave, and marking a past paper the student has already attempted. For a Year 9 in Kasarvadavali, start with a tutor in the room and move part of it online later, once the child has shown they will attempt work unsupervised.

faqs.question: What if our tutor and my child do not get along?
faqs.answer: Say so in week three and we change the tutor. This is the most common reason for a replacement and the least often reported, because parents treat it as a complaint rather than information. It is information. A sixteen-year-old who will not ask a question in front of a particular adult learns nothing, however well that adult knows the syllabus. The replacement comes from the same west Thane pool, receives the previous tutor's notes on what is secure and what is not, and starts with a short diagnostic rather than from the beginning.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with coursework or the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the skills a coursework component assesses, read the assessment criteria with the student, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, or replace the teacher who moderates it. For an alternative-to-practical written paper the help is different and quite teachable: reading an unfamiliar method off the page, spotting the control variable, handling tables and graphs, and writing the improvement that earns the mark. Confirm with the subject teacher what outside help your school permits before any coursework session.

faqs.question: How are predicted grades decided, and can tutoring change them?
faqs.answer: Predicted grades are set by the subject teachers from the evidence they hold, which is usually mock performance plus coursework to date, and no tutor can change one directly. What tutoring before the mocks can change is the evidence itself. This is the strongest practical argument for starting in September rather than February: a mock sat after a term of consistent work produces a different script, and the prediction follows the script. If the prediction has already gone out and matters for an application, speak to the school about their review process rather than to a tutor.

Session one is a diagnostic on the marked mock, and a written four-week plan follows within two days.
