sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the papers behind each IGCSE subject
paragraphs: An IGCSE subject is a set of papers and, in some subjects, a coursework or practical component that the school chooses at entry. Which route your child is on is not a detail you should guess: some syllabuses offer a practical examination or an alternative written paper, some offer coursework or an extra paper instead, and the choice has already been made by the department. Ask the subject teacher which route is on the entry, then tell the tutor.

Subject by subject the work looks different. Mathematics is paper technique and speed under a clock, with calculator rules set in the syllabus rather than by habit. English Language is two skills tested on paper and often a separate speaking component run inside school. Sciences split into content recall and the practical or alternative route. Business and Economics are data response plus structured writing, where a candidate who knows the content can still lose marks by answering the wrong command word.

Command words are where most of the recoverable marks sit, and they are teachable in a fortnight. Define, state, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate and justify each buy a different kind of sentence, and a Year 11 who writes a description when the paper asked for an evaluation has lost marks they knew the content for. A good tutor spends early sessions on this and can show you the improvement in a child's written answers inside a month, which is rare and checkable.

Supply is uneven by subject. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, English and Economics have a reasonable pool across South Mumbai. Computer Science, Business, Accounting, a second language or Art narrow it sharply, and that is where all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes in Sewri turn into a hybrid plan: a local tutor holding the weekly table session and a specialist joining online for the coursework or the paper-specific work. We would rather say that than send a confident generalist.
bullets: Confirm with the department whether the entry carries coursework or an extra paper.
Mathematics: technique and clock speed, with calculator rules from the syllabus.

sections.heading: The Sewri, Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel run at six in the evening
paragraphs: One tutor covers Sewri, Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel, and that is a deliberate limit rather than a shortage. IGCSE home tuition in Sewri works at 6pm and 7pm because those four addresses sit on short links and on the Harbour Line (CSMT–Dockyard–Sewri), so a tutor finishing in Parel is at a Sewri gate twenty minutes later. Widen the radius and the first cancellation arrives in week three.

The island is deceptive. A tutor leaving Worli for Colaba covers barely eight kilometres and can still arrive forty minutes later, because the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals do not care about the distance. South Mumbai is dense, short in kilometres and slow in minutes, which is why tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. The Western Line (Churchgate–Grant Road–Mumbai Central) half of South Mumbai is a weekend option for Sewri, not a Tuesday one.

By road, the Eastern Freeway is the useful artery: it brings a tutor from the Chembur and Wadala side into this corridor faster than the map suggests. The Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 (Aqua) Cuffe Parade–BKC have made the Churchgate end of the island reachable, which helps a Saturday morning more than a weekday evening. Parking is the other local variable, and on some of these lanes a tutor arriving by car is slower than one arriving by train.

The eastern waterfront is where this corridor changed. Sewri is now the island-city end of the Atal Setu, so Vashi, Nerul and Belapur sit a bridge away rather than an hour around the creek, and for the first time a Navi Mumbai specialist is a real option for families here. For mock-season intensives and for scarce subjects that is useful. For the standing weekday slot, we still match inside the island, and the next sections explain why.

sections.heading: Why mock season in Mumbai starts earlier than parents expect
paragraphs: International school terms here do not follow the state board rhythm, and the mock timetable is the proof. Children along this corridor attend campuses across the island city, with JBCN International School, Parel the nearest IB and IGCSE option for many Sewri families and Bombay International School serving the western side of South Mumbai. Each school sets its own mock window, and the earliest ones begin while parents still think of the winter as revision time.

Work backwards and the Year 11 calendar is tighter than it looks. Coursework and practical deadlines are set internally, well before any external date, because the department has to mark, moderate and upload. Mocks are then used by most schools as the evidence for tier entry and for predicted grades, which makes them a real event rather than a rehearsal. A child who treats the first mock as practice has handed the school its evidence anyway.

So the question to ask the school office in the first week of term is narrow: when are the mocks, when is the coursework due, and when does entry close. The examinations officer or the Head of Senior School has that sheet, and it is the single most useful document a Sewri family can hand a tutor. Everything a tutor plans, from past-paper order to the week they stop teaching content, keys off those three dates.

Schools are named here as local context only, with no relationship to this platform implied or intended. What matters to your plan is the pattern rather than the name: in a Mumbai international school, December and January carry mocks and coursework together, February is corrections and entry administration, and the external series follows. A tutor who starts in that February window is being asked to do a year's repair in a few weeks.

sections.heading: Is home tuition better than online for a Year 11 in Sewri?
paragraphs: For a Year 11 on this corridor, home tuition is the better default and online is the better supplement. An IGCSE home tutor in Sewri gets a child who is already seated, a phone that can be left in the next room, and the chance to watch a paper being attempted in real time under something close to exam conditions. That last part is hard to replicate on a screen, and it is where most mock marks are found.

Gate logistics decide whether the slot survives. Buildings along this corridor range from older low-rise blocks, where a word with the watchman is the whole protocol, to newer towers with a visitor register and a single working lift at 7pm. Ask the building office in week one to record the tutor as a standing weekly entry rather than a fresh visitor each time. Ten minutes lost at the gate and in the lift queue is a fifth of a session, every week, paid for.

The table matters as much as the tutor. Year 11 past-paper work needs a hard flat surface, a plug point, no television in earshot and a sibling who has been told. A bedroom with a closed door looks studious and hides a phone. If the flat has no workable corner at 7pm, say it on the call: an IGCSE online tutor in Sewri with a shared screen is better than a good tutor sitting in a room where nothing can be written.

Mock season is when hybrid earns its place. The pattern that works here is one home visit a week for teaching and one short online session for marking, where a scanned script can be annotated live and both board question banks are a click away. Online is weaker for a child who drifts without an adult present, and for working that has to be seen as the pen moves. Most families here run both by January.

sections.heading: What should I check myself before a tutor enters the building?
paragraphs: Three checks, and they take one phone call. Ask which board and tier the tutor's last students sat. Ask for a piece of written feedback on a past-paper answer with the student's name removed. Ask what they would do in the first three sessions for your specific subject. A tutor who answers all three concretely has taught the course; a tutor who answers in adjectives has not, and no document we hold will tell you that.

Our own checks sit underneath yours. Identity proof so you know who is entering your flat, degree documents in the subject claimed, and a teaching history verified by reference rather than by self-description. We record the boards each tutor works across, because many island-city tutors teach both IB and IGCSE and are stronger in one, and we note which tiers they have actually prepared candidates for. That last field is the one families here use most.

Red flags are consistent. Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, or who will not say which board's papers they use, or who wants a term paid upfront before a diagnostic session has happened. Be equally wary of a tutor who never sets written work: an IGCSE course is examined on paper, so a session that produces no writing has produced nothing you can check in a month.

What no verification can do is predict fit. We do not guarantee grades and we would not trust a platform that did. A fifteen-year-old who answers questions for one adult and waits out another is normal, and the honest response is a quick swap rather than a long conversation about effort. An IGCSE private tutor Sewri parents engage through us can be replaced after session two, which is the point at which most mismatches are already obvious.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: what changes for a Sewri family?
paragraphs: Your school chose the board, and you cannot change it, so the useful question is what the choice means for tutoring. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel cover similar content in most subjects and differ in how they ask for it: paper structure, the balance of short and extended questions, the way data and sources are presented, and the wording conventions in mark schemes. A tutor fluent in one and guessing at the other will teach good content and poor technique.

This matters most in the subjects where past papers are the teaching material. Mathematics, the sciences, Business and Economics are all learned by working through the right board's questions in the right order, and the question banks are not interchangeable. When a tutor says they teach to both, ask which board the last three students sat, and whether they keep separate mark-scheme notes. The honest ones will say they are stronger in one, which is a better answer than easy confidence.

Island-city supply is lopsided here, and this is where the bridge matters. Tutors with deep Pearson Edexcel experience in a scarce subject are harder to find inside South Mumbai than Cambridge specialists, and before the Atal Setu the practical answer was an online tutor nobody had met. Now a specialist living in Vashi, Nerul or Belapur can cross for a Saturday double session while a tutor from Wadala or Parel holds the weekday slot, which keeps both technique and frequency.

A worked case from this corridor. A Year 11 in Sewri sitting Business at Extended tier, with coursework already submitted and mocks in five weeks, needs data-response drilling on her own board's papers rather than more content. The plan that works is a Parel tutor twice a week for the content gaps and a Navi Mumbai subject specialist across the bridge on two Saturdays for paper technique. Two tutors, one plan, and the family keeps the weekday slot intact.

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one mock cycle: reading progress in Mumbai
paragraphs: Four weeks buys you evidence about process, not grades. By then your child should be attempting past-paper questions before the session rather than during it, and the tutor should have told you one specific thing about the written answers that the school had not: a command-word habit, a missing working step, an answer that runs out of time on the last question. Nothing specific after four sessions means the match is wrong.

One term in, look at a marked script rather than a report. Longer answers should now be structured, the easy marks at the start of a paper should stop leaking, and the child should be able to say why an answer scored what it scored. A school report written in December reflects work from October, so treat it as a lagging signal and ask the tutor in week eight to predict what it will say. A tutor who is badly wrong is not reading the work.

Across a full mock cycle the honest statement is that tutoring changes the quality of what gets written and the rate at which technique improves, while the result depends on sleep, the school's teaching, which questions appear and how the paper is moderated. We do not guarantee grades, we do not publish success rates, and we do not think anybody in Mumbai can honestly do either. Progress you can see on a script is the thing worth paying for.

IGCSE tuition fees in Sewri depend on five things and none of them is a list price. The board and tier, since Extended paper technique in a scarce subject costs more to supply than Core support. Subject scarcity. Travel distance and the hour, because a 7pm island slot eats a tutor's whole evening. Session length. And frequency, which rises near mocks, so budget for the January surge rather than being surprised by it.

sections.heading: Setting up IGCSE home classes in Sewri before the next mock
paragraphs: Four documents make the first session productive, and the school has three of them. The subject list with syllabus codes, because a tutor needs to know exactly which syllabus is on the entry. The mock and coursework date sheet. The most recent marked script, annotations intact. And your own two protected evenings, written down before you talk to anybody, including the week the school trip or a family wedding takes one of them out.

Pick the slot first, then the tutor. On this corridor a 7pm start survives the term and a 6pm start does not, because school transport arrives later as the monsoon term wears on and nobody rebuilds the timetable in August. Tell us the two evenings and we shortlist against them. Families who choose the tutor first and negotiate the time afterwards are the families who lose a session a fortnight by October.

The diagnostic session has a shape worth expecting. The tutor reads the marked script, sets one question from the right board and tier under a clock, watches how your child reads the stem, and then tells you what the first month covers. You should hear a specific diagnosis: time lost on the first page, working not shown, a command word misread repeatedly. Reassurance without a named weakness means the tutor has not looked closely enough.

After that, ask for three lines a week by message: what we covered, what is set, what I am watching. Those three lines are how a parent stays ahead of a Year 11 without standing in the doorway. If they stop arriving, the engagement has gone quiet and that is your signal to call us. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hire through this platform is expected to send them without being chased.

faqs.question: Should my child take Core or Extended in Mathematics?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the subject teacher in Year 10, made on written evidence, and the school submits the entry against its own deadline. Extended opens the upper grade range and asks harder questions; Core is a genuine route for a child who will otherwise lose the subject entirely. What a tutor can do is make the evidence clear by Year 10: if the Extended questions are reachable with better technique rather than a different brain, that shows up in a marked script inside a term. Ask the teacher what evidence they are waiting for, then work on exactly that.

faqs.question: Do fees change between Core and Extended, or during mock season?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and for practical reasons rather than pricing strategy. IGCSE tuition fees in Sewri track the board and tier, subject scarcity, travel distance, session length and frequency. Extended technique in a thin-supply subject such as Accounting or a second language costs more to source than Core support in Mathematics. Mock season raises the total because families add a third session or a weekend intensive, not because the hourly rate moves. Agree the frequency change in December rather than discovering it in January, and ask each shortlisted tutor what they would charge for the pre-mock fortnight.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach my building in Sewri twice a week for an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the tutor lives inside the island city. Two weekday sessions at 6pm or 7pm work from Wadala, Mazgaon, Parel or Dadar, because those are short runs that do not depend on a clear main road. They stop working when a tutor commits to coming from the western or far eastern suburbs in the evening peak: the arrival time drifts by week three and the second session is the one that gets dropped. We shortlist on realistic travel rather than on stated willingness.

faqs.question: How does the gate pass and visitor register work for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Settle it once in the first week. Give the building office the tutor's name and number and ask for a standing weekly entry instead of a fresh visitor pass each session. Older blocks on this corridor need nothing more than a word with the watchman. Newer towers log every visitor and will hold a tutor at the gate until somebody in the flat answers a phone, which costs ten minutes of a sixty-minute session plus the lift queue at 7pm. Tell the tutor which entrance and which lift to use.

faqs.question: My school teaches Pearson Edexcel. Does the tutor have to match?
faqs.answer: For subjects taught through past papers, yes, it matters. Pearson Edexcel and Cambridge International Education ask for similar content in different shapes, and the mark-scheme conventions differ enough that technique coaching from the wrong board is partly wasted. Ask a shortlisted tutor which board the last three candidates they prepared actually sat, and whether they keep separate notes for each. A tutor who says they are stronger in one board is being honest; one who treats them as interchangeable will teach good content and leave marks on the table.

faqs.question: When do mocks happen, and when should tuition start?
faqs.answer: Mock windows are set school by school, and many Mumbai international schools run them across December and January alongside internal coursework deadlines. Ask your examinations officer for the dates in the first week of term rather than assuming. Working backwards, the comfortable start is early in Year 10 or the opening term of Year 11, which leaves time for content and technique. A February start is repair work: possible, useful, and far more stressful than beginning the same programme six months earlier.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in the middle of Year 11?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. A mid-Year 11 start means triage: the tutor picks the two or three topics with the highest mark yield, drills command words and timing, and leaves the rest. That is a legitimate strategy and it produces visible improvement on a script, which is what mocks measure. What it cannot do is rebuild two years of missed content. Be clear with the tutor in the first session that you want triage rather than coverage, and ask which topics they are deliberately skipping.

faqs.question: What if my child's coursework is already overdue?
faqs.answer: Speak to the school today, before the tutor. Coursework deadlines are internal and the department has moderation and upload work to do afterwards, so an extension is the school's decision and nobody else's. A tutor's role is narrow and important: helping your child plan the remaining work, reading a draft for structure and asking whether the question can be answered in the length available. A tutor who starts writing or rewriting the coursework has created an academic honesty problem that is far worse than a late submission.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for IGCSE past-paper practice?
faqs.answer: It works well for marking and badly for supervision. A shared screen is the best way to annotate a scanned script line by line, and both boards' question banks are instantly to hand, so online is strong for feedback sessions. It is weak when a child needs someone in the room to stop a phone appearing, and for subjects where the tutor has to watch working as it is written. The pattern most families on this corridor settle into is one session at home each week plus one online marking slot.

faqs.question: Is a Saturday mock intensive worth bringing a tutor across the Atal Setu?
faqs.answer: For a scarce subject, often yes. Sewri sits at the island-city end of the Atal Setu, so a specialist in Vashi, Nerul or Belapur is a bridge run away rather than an hour around the creek, and a Saturday morning double session on paper technique is a sensible use of that. For weekday evenings we still match inside the island, because a tutor leaving Navi Mumbai at 6pm in the peak will be late often enough to cost you the slot. Keep the bridge for weekends and the local tutor for weeknights.

faqs.question: We live in Sewri but my child studies in Parel. Does that change the tutor?
faqs.answer: It changes the timing rather than the person. The pool for Sewri, Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel is a single pool, so the same tutors appear whichever of those addresses you search from, and queries like IGCSE tutors near me in Sewri surface the same names as a Parel search. What changes is the return journey: a child coming home through Parel traffic arrives later than one walking in from a nearby school, so build the slot at 7pm and keep it fixed for the term.

sections.heading: How a request for IGCSE home tuition in Sion becomes a shortlist
paragraphs: The matching problem at this level is narrower than parents expect, which is good news. An IGCSE student is in a two-year run with a known endpoint, so the useful question is not "who teaches well" but "who has taken students through this exact syllabus code at this exact tier and seen the examiner reports". A tutor who has taught Cambridge Biology 0610 at Extended tier through three exam series knows which structured questions eat marks and why. A tutor who has taught the same content in a different system, however competently, is guessing. We filter on that first and on everything else second.

The sequence is short enough to hold us to. 1. You tell us the board, the syllabus codes if you have them from the school, the year group and the subjects that are actually a problem. 2. We filter for tutors with that board and tier in their teaching history, then narrow to the ones whose own travel into Sion makes a standing weekday slot realistic across a full term. 3. Two or three profiles come back with board, subject and series history attached. 4. You take a free discovery call with the tutor who would teach. 5. The first lesson follows only if you say yes, and we come back to you after two to four weeks to ask whether the specific thing you hired for has moved.

The brief that gets results is specific about the failure, not about the ambition. "Year 11, Cambridge, Mathematics Extended and Chemistry, scoring well on recall questions and losing most of the marks on the longer structured ones, Monday and Wednesday evenings" tells a specialist what the first fortnight contains. "Needs help with science" produces a phone call and a delay. The brief is the whole of what an IGCSE home tutor in Sion has to work from before meeting your child, so spend fifteen minutes on it. If you have the last report and two pieces of marked work, send those instead of describing them. A tutor reads a teacher's marginal comments faster and more accurately than any parent can summarise them, and the comments are usually where the real diagnosis sits.

Session one should be spent diagnosing under exam conditions rather than teaching. The method that works is simple: the tutor gives the student a short set of past-paper questions on topics already covered, watches them attempt it without help, and then reads the attempt against the mark scheme line by line. Within an hour that produces a list of causes rather than symptoms, which is the difference between "weak at Chemistry" and "loses marks because the answer never states the observation before the conclusion". The second of those is fixable in a fortnight. The first is not even a problem statement.

sections.heading: Is your child sitting a Cambridge or a Pearson Edexcel IGCSE?
paragraphs: Ask the school and write down the answer, because the two are not interchangeable and a tutor who assumes the wrong one will waste a month. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both offer an International General Certificate of Secondary Education, and most schools in Mumbai run one or the other, occasionally mixing subjects across both. The syllabus content overlaps heavily. The paper structures, the command words in the mark schemes, the way practical work is assessed and the specimen material a student should be practising on do not overlap nearly as much, and it is in those differences that marks are lost.

Cambridge subjects carry a four-digit syllabus code, which is the single most useful piece of information you can get from the school. Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450, English as a Second Language 0510: the number tells a tutor exactly which specimen papers and which examiner reports to work from. Pearson Edexcel uses a different code system for its International GCSE subjects. Either way, a specialist asks for the code in the first conversation. A generalist asks what the textbook is called, which tells them far less than they think it does.

The second structural thing to understand is that this is a terminal assessment system. Unlike a programme with a large internally assessed component, most IGCSE subjects are decided in a short window of written papers at the end, with a practical or an alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences and coursework in a smaller number of subjects. Consequently a student who knows the material and cannot perform it under timed conditions loses real marks, and a student who is shaky on content but drilled on technique often outperforms them. That asymmetry is why the final two terms of a Year 11 should look almost nothing like the first two terms of a Year 9.

One more thing families here ask about constantly, and it belongs in this section rather than buried: what happens after Year 11. Some students move into a Diploma Programme, some into A Levels, some into an Indian board stream. A student who takes Mathematics at the lower tier will find certain senior-year routes harder to enter, and that conversation is better had in Year 9 than in the fortnight when the next form is due.

sections.heading: The tier decision, the practical papers and the subjects parents underestimate
paragraphs: The Core and Extended tier decision is the most consequential academic choice in these two years, and it is frequently made on the basis of one term's marks in Year 9. Extended covers additional content and asks harder questions; Core covers less and caps the grade range available. Schools generally enter students where they are currently performing, which is reasonable, and parents generally want Extended, which is also reasonable. The useful question is neither of those. It is whether the specific gaps holding the student at Core level are fixable in the time remaining, and that is a question a subject specialist can answer honestly in about three sessions of looking at real work.

In the sciences, the practical component is where otherwise strong students quietly lose marks. Depending on the school's entry, a student sits either a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper, and both test a particular kind of thinking: reading an apparatus diagram, identifying the variable being controlled, spotting why a method would not produce reliable data, describing an observation in the language the mark scheme wants. None of that is taught by revising content. It is taught by working through past practical papers with someone who knows how those answers are credited, which is a narrow and genuinely scarce skill among tutors.

The subjects parents underestimate are the language and humanities ones, and the pattern is consistent. English as a Second Language and First Language English are heavily technique-driven: a student who reads well can still lose marks on a summary question by including material the question did not ask for. Business Studies and Economics punish students who write what they know rather than answering the command word, so an "analyse" question answered with a description scores a fraction of what it could. History and Geography reward structured argument and source handling over memory. In every one of these, the fix is rewriting answers against a mark scheme, not rereading notes.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Sion is likely to be asked for, the request we see most is Mathematics plus one science, usually in Year 10 or early Year 11. That combination is the easiest to staff well and the most responsive to a term of focused work, because both reward method and both have abundant past-paper material. Do not take paper structures or component details from this page. Boards revise specifications on their own cycle, so get the current structure from your school's coordinator or the live syllabus document, and use a tutor to work out what your child specifically is losing marks on.

sections.heading: Getting to Sion: Matunga, Wadala, Kurla and the SCLR
paragraphs: Sion is grouped with South Mumbai administratively but behaves like a hinge between the island city and the eastern suburbs, and for scheduling purposes the hinge is what matters. The locality sits at the Sion–Dharavi junction, with Sion station on the Central Line, Matunga immediately north, Wadala to the south on the Harbour Line, and Kurla the next large interchange heading up the line. The Santacruz–Chembur Link Road, the SCLR, meets the area from the east. A tutor living in Chembur or Powai can therefore be at a flat near Sion station in under half an hour, which does not happen for an address in Colaba or Breach Candy.

That matters because of what the rest of the island is like. South Mumbai is dense and short in distance but slow in practice, and a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers roughly eight kilometres while still losing a large part of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. The working rule across the island is that tutors are matched within it rather than brought down from the suburbs, and families further south live with a narrower pool because of it. Sion is the exception rather than the rule, and a parent here should push for a subject specialist rather than accepting the nearest generalist.

Each neighbouring area contributes a different kind of availability. Matunga is close enough that a tutor can hold a six o'clock start on a weekday without gambling on traffic, which matters for Year 9 and Year 10 students who still have energy early in the evening. Wadala connects south through the Eastern Freeway and works well for tutors who want two sessions on one evening run. Kurla is where the Central and Harbour lines meet, so tutors travelling in from Ghatkopar, Chembur or further up the line pass through it already. Between the three, an IGCSE home tutor in Sion is almost always arriving over a short route rather than a long one.

Two scheduling habits protect the arrangement through the year. Fix the day and the time and then defend them, because a tutor who builds a weekly route around a standing Wednesday in Sion will protect that slot, while one who is asked to float between evenings will eventually fill the gap with someone else. And push the start time off the worst of the peak if your child can take it. The window from roughly half past six to half past eight is when every approach road in this part of Mumbai is at its worst, and moving to a 5.45pm or a 8.30pm start removes the most common reason a tutor arrives late, flustered and twenty minutes short.

sections.heading: Why does the Mumbai school year decide when you should hire?
paragraphs: Because the work an IGCSE tutor can do changes completely depending on which month you start, and most parents start in the worst one. Hire in June or July and a tutor has a clear run at foundations while nothing is urgent, which is when the real repair work happens. Hire in late November, after the first set of serious reports, and you are asking someone to rebuild a year of gaps during the weeks when mocks, coursework deadlines and revision are all live at once. The content taught is identical. The amount of it that lands is not remotely the same.

Families in and around Sion send children to a spread of schools rather than one dominant institution. Don Bosco International School and Witty International School both serve this part of Mumbai, and others travel to Parel, Chembur or Bandra Kurla Complex, which is why the commute-friendly geography of this junction counts twice: once for the school run in the morning and once for the tutor's route in the evening. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with any school named here. We name them because their internal calendars, not ours, set the deadlines a tutor has to plan around. Most IGCSE home classes in Sion are therefore built around a school timetable written somewhere else in Mumbai entirely.

The pressure points repeat every year and are worth putting in a calendar. The early months after a new year begins are quiet and underused. The middle of the year brings the first coursework and practical deadlines in the subjects that carry them, along with the first proper assessments that generate the reports parents react to. December and January are mock examination season, and mocks are the most useful diagnostic a family gets all year because they are marked against real schemes. February through April is the final run at past papers before the main series, and by then a tutor is managing technique and nerves more than content.

Here is how that looks for one household rather than in the abstract. A Year 11 student living near Sion station, entered at Extended tier for Mathematics and two sciences, sits mocks in the same month that a Business Studies coursework draft is due and a younger sibling's assessments land. Nothing in that list is unreasonable on its own. Together they are a sequencing problem, and the tutor who earns their fee in that month is the one who sits down with a calendar, decides which paper gets a full effort and which gets a competent one, and makes sure the student is practising under timed conditions rather than reading notes at midnight.

sections.heading: Home classes, online or both for an IGCSE student in Sion
paragraphs: Start with home classes and treat online as a deliberate choice rather than a default. The reason is specific to this level: a great deal of IGCSE improvement comes from watching a student write an answer and intervening while they write it. A tutor sitting next to a Year 10 student can see the moment the working stops, the diagram that is never drawn, the question read too fast. On a screen, most of that is invisible, and a student who has learned to narrate confidently can hide a lot. For a student heading into a terminal exam series, that visibility is worth more than convenience, which is why IGCSE home tuition in Sion is what we recommend first and online second.

Online earns its place in three identifiable situations. The first is scarcity: if your child needs a less commonly taught subject, or Pearson Edexcel specifically when most nearby tutors teach Cambridge, then an IGCSE online tutor in Sion who genuinely knows that specification beats a nearby tutor who does not. The second is the final six weeks before papers, when three short focused sessions a week beat two long ones and travel time becomes the binding constraint. The third is the monsoon, which does more damage to standing arrangements across Mumbai than any other single cause and is entirely predictable.

The hybrid pattern most of our longer arrangements settle into is worth designing on purpose. One longer in-person session a week handles the work that needs a tutor in the room: marking written answers together, past-paper attempts under observation, practical method questions worked through with the apparatus diagram on the table. A shorter mid-week online session handles question-setting, doubt clearing and a check that the agreed task was actually done. The second contact point is what stops the week resetting, and because it is short and involves no travel it survives a late evening at work or a changed school commitment.

The honest trade-offs deserve stating. Home sessions carry a tutor's unpaid travel, which is priced in whether the invoice shows it or not, and they are the first thing that breaks when the roads do. Online sessions only work if someone at your end cares about the setup: a door that closes, a real screen rather than a phone, and a tutor who insists the student photographs and shares written work instead of reading answers aloud. Hybrid is the most robust and the most administratively irritating. Choose for this child and this week rather than for whichever mode sounds more serious to an adult.

sections.heading: What should you ask an IGCSE tutor on the first call?
paragraphs: Three questions separate a specialist from a generalist in about four minutes. Which board, syllabus code and tier did you teach most recently, and in which exam series? How would you spend the first session with my child? What would you show me after four weeks to prove something had changed? A tutor who has done this work answers all three concretely, with a code, a method and a specific artefact. A tutor who has not answers in adjectives about rapport and dedication. Both conversations feel pleasant. Only one of them tells you anything.

Our own checks run before you ever see a profile, in a fixed order. Identity first: government photo identification, a working number, an address we have actually confirmed. Qualifications second, read against the documents rather than the claim, and specifically matched against the board and level the tutor says they teach. Teaching history third, and this is where the time goes, because the gap between "I teach IGCSE" and "I have taken Extended tier Chemistry students through three exam series and can describe what the practical paper does to their marks" is the whole point of the exercise. What we cannot test for is whether this adult suits your child, which is what the discovery call is for.

The warning signs are worth more than any credential. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because nobody controls what happens in an examination hall and the people who say otherwise are selling a package. Be equally careful of the tutor who wants a large block of sessions paid before you have seen one lesson, the one who will not commit the weekly slot to writing, and the one who opens by telling you the school is teaching the subject incorrectly. An IGCSE private tutor in Sion who is confident about their work is relaxed about starting with a single session.

Then run your own checks, which take almost no time and reveal more than ours. Be in the flat for session one if you can. Read the first piece of work that comes back marked and ask whether the comments are specific enough to act on this week. Ask your child after the second session what they are now supposed to be doing differently, because a child who cannot answer that has been taught at rather than taught. Parents looking for the best IGCSE tutor in Sion usually imagine the answer is a qualification. It is far more often a match, and the first fortnight is when you can see it.

sections.heading: Why do past papers matter more at IGCSE than anywhere else?
paragraphs: Because the grade is decided almost entirely by performance in a short window of written papers, and those papers are remarkably consistent in how they ask things. A student who has worked through several series of past papers under timed conditions has met the question types, the phrasing, the diagram conventions and the traps. A student who has revised the same content from notes has met none of them. This is not a shortcut or a gaming of the system. It is the difference between knowing chemistry and being able to demonstrate knowing chemistry in six marks under time pressure, and the examiners are explicitly testing the second thing.

Used properly, a past paper is a diagnostic instrument rather than practice. The method that works has four steps. First, the student attempts a paper or a section under real time constraints with no help and no notes. Second, they mark it themselves against the official mark scheme before the tutor says anything, which is where most of the learning happens because the mark scheme shows what the examiner wanted rather than what the student assumed. Third, the tutor and student classify every lost mark: content not known, method not shown, command word misread, time ran out, careless slip. Fourth, the next fortnight targets whichever category is largest. Most students discover that content is the smallest of the five.

The classification step is the one almost nobody does, and it is where the leverage is. A Year 11 student losing eighteen marks on a Mathematics Extended paper may have lost three to unknown content and fifteen to not showing method, misreading "hence", and running out of time on the last question. Those are three different problems with three different fixes, and none of them is solved by another week of revising topics. An honest tutor will tell you this in session two and will show you the tally, which also happens to be the best evidence you will get that the arrangement is working. Ask for it by name when you start IGCSE home tuition in Sion, because a tutor who keeps the tally cannot drift into vague reassurance.

Two cautions. Doing papers without marking them properly is close to worthless, and plenty of students do exactly that because it feels productive. And the papers must match the current specification, since boards revise their syllabuses and an old paper can test content no longer examined or omit something now central. A good tutor curates which papers are still valid rather than handing over a folder of everything available. The list of all IB and IGCSE subjects an IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai families hire tends to cover is long, but the method above transfers across nearly all of it.

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term and one exam series in Mumbai
paragraphs: Four weeks of an IGCSE home tutor in Sion is about six to eight sessions, and the evidence you should expect at that point is not a better grade. It is three things. The tutor can name the specific causes of lost marks and show you the tally. Your child can say, without being prompted, what they are doing differently. And at least one returned piece of work demonstrates the change, even if the mark has moved only slightly. Four weeks is long enough to fix a method and short enough that nothing structural has been rebuilt. Anyone promising more than that in a month is managing your expectations in the wrong direction.

At one term, roughly twelve weeks, the mark should have moved and the movement should be explainable in one sentence. A student who was losing marks for not showing method should be losing fewer for exactly that reason. A student who was running out of time should be finishing papers. A coursework piece should be genuinely in progress rather than perpetually about to start. If a full term has gone by and nobody can point to a specific change, the arrangement has become a weekly habit rather than teaching, and that is the week to have an awkward conversation instead of waiting for the next report card.

At one exam series, the honest claim is narrower than this industry likes to pretend. A good tutor raises the floor: fewer careless losses, answers that address the command word, papers finished, work submitted in the right form and on time, a student who walks in having practised under timed conditions rather than having reread notes. That is a real and often substantial difference. It is not a promise about a number. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because the outcome depends on the student in the hall, the paper that comes up and a dozen things nobody controls.

When the fit is wrong, say so in week two or three. The usual causes are all identifiable and fixable at that stage: the board or tier match is slightly off, the slot sits at the end of a day when your child has nothing left, the subject is right but the level is not, or the personalities simply do not work. A replacement carries no penalty and is more common than parents assume. There is also the version nobody enjoys hearing: sometimes the teaching is fine and the problem is sleep, an undiagnosed learning difference or a subject the student should never have been entered for, and a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai can supply will not fix any of those three.

sections.heading: Booking your first IGCSE home classes in Sion
paragraphs: Four pieces of information turn an enquiry into a shortlist, and gathering them takes fifteen minutes. The board, which the school will confirm, and the syllabus codes if they are on the report. The year group and the exact subjects that are a problem, separated from the ones that are fine. The last report plus two pieces of marked work, sent as photographs rather than described. And the two weekly slots you can hold for a full term, including the one you would rather not offer. Parents who send these get profiles that fit on the first pass. Parents who send a subject name get a phone call and lose a few days.

What happens next is deliberately unexciting. We read the brief, filter for board and tier, filter again for tutors whose travel into Sion works at the hour you need, and send two or three profiles with real series history. You choose who to speak to. The discovery call is free, it is with the tutor rather than a coordinator, and it is the place to ask the three questions from the verification section. If the call goes well, one first session is booked. If it does not, you say so and someone else comes forward. No package is paid for in advance and nothing is locked in.

The first session has a shape you can hold a tutor to. A timed attempt at past-paper questions on topics already taught. A read-through of that attempt against the mark scheme, out loud, with the student present. Then a plan: the largest category of lost marks, two or three targets for the fortnight, and one task to do before the next session. You should receive a short written note afterwards saying what was found and what was set. If a tutor cannot produce that after ninety minutes with your child's work, it is better to know on day one than in week six.

One practical note for the first fortnight. Tell your building's security desk that a named tutor will be arriving on the same day and at the same time every week, and give the tutor the entrance to use and a number to call. The most common cause of a lost first session anywhere in Mumbai is a tutor standing outside a gate while an intercom goes unanswered. Agree in advance what happens if a session has to move, because agreeing it after you need it never goes as well. Families who sort this in week one rarely lose a slot later in the year.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Sion cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things, and we publish no rate card because one number for every IGCSE home tutor in Sion across every board and subject would mislead you. faqs.answer: Yes, and the geography here helps more than it does elsewhere on the island. faqs.question: My child's school has not decided Core or Extended yet. Should we wait?
faqs.answer: No, start now, because the tier decision itself is one of the things a tutor can usefully inform. Send the last two pieces of marked work and let a specialist spend three sessions establishing whether the gaps holding your child at Core level are fixable in the time available. That is a far better basis for the conversation with school than a parent's hope or a single term's mark. Waiting until the entry is made removes your influence over it entirely and leaves you reacting to a decision rather than contributing to it.

faqs.question: Do you have Pearson Edexcel specialists, or only Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Both, listed separately, because they are not interchangeable. Say which board your child's school uses in your first message and the shortlist will reflect it. The content overlaps substantially between the two, but the paper structures, command words, mark schemes and specimen material differ enough that a tutor working from the wrong specification wastes a month. This is also the single most common place where a nearby generalist loses to a slightly further specialist working online.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 student need?
faqs.answer: Two per subject in the final two terms is the pattern that works most often for IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai, and one per subject earlier. The reason is contact frequency rather than total hours: two shorter sessions give a student a mid-week checkpoint, which is what stops a week from quietly resetting. One long session a week tends to become a catch-up on work that was not done. In the final six weeks before papers, three short sessions often beat two long ones, which is also when a mid-week online session earns its place over a second journey across Mumbai.

faqs.question: Which areas around Sion do your tutors come from?
faqs.answer: Mostly Matunga, Wadala, Kurla, Chembur and Dadar, with some travelling from Powai along the SCLR. Matunga tutors hold early starts most reliably because the trip is short enough that a six o'clock session is realistic midweek. Wadala connects south through the Eastern Freeway, so a Wadala-based tutor can sometimes take a Sion slot and a second one further south on the same evening. Kurla is where the Central and Harbour lines meet, which means tutors from further up the line already pass through it on their way.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get into our building for a weekly evening visit?
faqs.answer: Usually, if it is set up once rather than negotiated weekly. Tell your society office or security desk that a named tutor will arrive on the same day and at the same time each week, and give the tutor the correct entrance plus a number to call. The commonest cause of a lost first session anywhere in Mumbai is a tutor waiting outside a gate while nobody answers the intercom. Families who handle this in the first week almost never lose a slot afterwards. Those who leave it informal lose roughly one session a quarter.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for IGCSE science practicals?
faqs.answer: For the practical paper itself, partially; for the alternative-to-practical paper, genuinely well. The alternative paper tests reading apparatus diagrams, identifying controlled variables, spotting unreliable method and describing observations in mark-scheme language, all of which work on a screen with the diagram shared. A hands-on practical examination is harder to prepare remotely and benefits from a tutor in the room. Ask the school which your child is entered for before deciding, because the answer changes the recommendation completely and parents often assume the wrong one.

faqs.question: What if we are not happy with the tutor after three weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, with no penalty and no uncomfortable negotiation. Three weeks is the right moment, not the end of term. The usual causes are identifiable: the board or tier match is slightly off, the slot falls when your child has nothing left, or the personalities do not fit. None of those improve by waiting politely. A change in week three costs one week of momentum. The same change in month four costs a term of it, and the examination date does not move to accommodate the delay.

faqs.question: Which schools near Sion do the families you work with use?
faqs.answer: A spread rather than one or two. Don Bosco International School and Witty International School both serve this part of Mumbai, and other families travel to Parel, Chembur or Bandra Kurla Complex. We name schools only as local context, because their internal calendars set the coursework and mock dates a tutor has to plan around. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of them. What matters in practice is the school's own assessment timetable, which is almost always earlier than the external one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects for the same child?
faqs.answer: For some combinations, yes, and Mathematics with Physics is the pairing that works most often because the method overlaps heavily. Mathematics with a language rarely works well, because genuine depth in both is uncommon and you end up with a specialist in one and a generalist in the other. The honest test is whether the tutor has recent teaching history at this tier in both. If they have it in one, use them for that and take a second tutor for the other rather than accepting a compromise that costs marks.

faqs.question: When is the best time of year to start?
faqs.answer: June or July, which is the opposite of when most parents search. Those weeks are quiet, nothing is urgent, and a tutor can spend a month on foundations and method without fighting a deadline. You also get first choice of the tutors who live close enough to hold the slot. Starting in late November means competing with every other family in Mumbai reacting to the same reports, and asking a tutor to repair a year of gaps during the exact weeks when mocks and coursework deadlines are already running.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, Core or Extended: the entries that set the ceiling
paragraphs: Two boards dominate the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) in Mumbai: Cambridge International Education, and Pearson Edexcel with its International GCSE. They are not interchangeable. The subject lists differ, the paper structures differ, the availability of coursework differs, and a tutor who has taught one fluently can still misread the other's mark scheme. Ask which board your child is entered for before you ask anything else, and ask the tutor which board they have actually taught.

Inside several Cambridge subjects there is a second decision: tier. Core and Extended are different papers with different content and different reachable grade ranges. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades no matter how well they perform, which is a reasonable choice for some children and a quiet disaster for a child who is capable of Extended and was entered conservatively in Year 9 after one bad term. Pearson Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher in a comparable way in some subjects.

This is the single most consequential thing parents in Tardeo do not know they are deciding. Entry decisions are made by the school, usually well before the examination series, and they are changeable only up to a point. If your child's tutor says in January that the Extended papers are within reach, that conversation needs to go to the school quickly rather than at the end of the term.

Grading language is also changing: some schools report the numeric scale alongside the older letter grades. Do not take any structure from a page like this as settled. Ask your school's IGCSE coordinator for the current syllabus and the entry deadlines for your child's cohort, because boards revise both.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the components that quietly lose marks
paragraphs: Across IGCSE subjects the marks leak in predictable places, and almost none of them are pure content. In the sciences it is the practical component: either a laboratory paper or the alternative-to-practical route, depending on the subject and the school. Students who can describe an experiment in words still lose marks for not stating a control, not identifying a source of error, or drawing a graph with an unlabelled axis. These are teachable habits, and a term of deliberate practice moves them.

In Mathematics the loss is method marks. A student who writes only the answer surrenders everything when the answer is wrong, and the fix is behavioural rather than mathematical. In English the loss is in the directed-writing and reading-response work, where students summarise when they were asked to analyse tone, or write beautifully about the wrong half of the extract. In Business, Economics and the humanities it is command words: describe, explain, analyse and evaluate are instructions with different mark structures behind them, and students treat them as synonyms.

Where coursework is offered, the pattern is different again. Coursework rewards planning and revision over fluency, which suits some students and frustrates others, and a tutor's job on a coursework component is mostly to teach drafting discipline rather than content. Subject choice interacts with this: a student who writes slowly under pressure may do better in a subject with a coursework route.

Families often begin by asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Tardeo can cover, or for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Tardeo schedules allow in one evening. Our internal listing for that broad request reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai, and it is accurate and nearly useless. Two subjects, two specialists, is almost always the better arrangement.

Mathematics: writing only the answer forfeits every method mark

sections.heading: How far will an IGCSE tutor come from Tardeo into Mumbai's southern pockets?
paragraphs: Roughly as far as the evening traffic allows, which in this part of Mumbai is a short way. A tutor working from Tardeo comfortably covers Peddar Road, Mahalaxmi and Cumballa Hill, and that is the honest radius rather than a brochure one. Peddar Road looks like a two-minute journey and behaves like a twenty-minute one once the southbound evening flow builds, because there is no second road to take.

Mahalaxmi connects families to the Western Line through its own station and Mumbai Central, which matters when a tutor travels by train rather than car. Cumballa Hill sits above the Tardeo junction, quiet and close, and tutors who already teach a child there will take a Tardeo slot without negotiating, because the walk is shorter than the lift ride. Grant Road is the other nearby station, and the Tardeo-Jaslok corridor is the spine the whole arrangement runs along.

An IGCSE private tutor Tardeo families keep for two years is almost always someone who was already teaching within a kilometre or two when you found them. That is not a coincidence. A tutor who agrees to travel from the Western Suburbs for a seven o'clock lesson is agreeing to something that works in a dry September and collapses in July, and the collapse always arrives in the term that matters.

Metro Line 3 has altered the southern commute and the Coastal Road has altered the western one, which helps tutors reach the island from further away for a weekend lesson. Neither has touched the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals at the evening peak, so weekday slots are still a local matter. paragraphs: Aditya Birla World Academy sits in Tardeo and enters students for both IGCSE and the IB Diploma Programme. For a tutor planning a year here, that is unusual and useful. The practical effect on IGCSE tutoring is about front-loading. If a tutor knows in September which fortnight the school fills with mocks and internal assessment submissions, they can finish teaching new content before it and spend that fortnight on past papers instead of starting a topic nobody has time for. Tutors working across many schools cannot plan that precisely, and the difference shows in February.

The flip side is congestion. sections.heading: Is home tuition in Tardeo better than online for Years 9 to 11?
paragraphs: For most Year 9 and 10 students, yes, and the reason is supervision rather than teaching quality. A fifteen-year-old working on a mock paper at the dining table with a tutor beside them cannot drift. The same student on a video call has a second tab. IGCSE home tuition in Tardeo also lets a tutor read the written work directly, which matters enormously in a system where method marks and annotation habits decide outcomes. Handwriting on a shared screen hides exactly what you need to see.

An IGCSE online tutor in Tardeo earns their place in two situations. The first is a scarce subject: if your child is entered for a less commonly taught language, or for a specification the island's tutors rarely teach, the right board-experienced specialist may be in another city, and that specialist beats a local generalist. The second is the final run-in, where several short paper-marking sessions a week are more useful than one long lesson and nobody wants a tutor stuck in the evening peak twice a week.

Hybrid is where most arrangements land by the second term. The teaching lesson happens at home; past-paper marking and quick clinics happen online. We think hybrid is the most durable shape for home classes in Mumbai, because it absorbs a school trip, a cold and a traffic failure without the teaching stopping.

The honest trade-off is attention versus access. Online buys you the best available tutor for the specification. Home buys you the student actually doing the work for the full hour. For Years 9 to 11, most families should weight the second more heavily than they expect to.

sections.heading: Vetting an IGCSE tutor: what we check and what only you can see
paragraphs: IB Gram verifies identity against government photographic identification, confirms the degree or teaching qualification a tutor claims, and takes up teaching history by board, subject and tier. If someone says they have taught Cambridge Extended Mathematics for years, they can name the schools and the cohorts. Claims about examining or marking experience are recorded as claims until documented, because that particular claim is the one most often inflated in this market.

What verification cannot capture is whether this person can teach your child. Three checks are yours. Ask for one topic to be taught in the trial lesson, not described, and watch whether the tutor asks questions or lectures. Ask them to mark one page of your child's work in front of you and explain the marks lost, which separates people who know the specification from people who know the subject. And be wary of any tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because the offer itself is the warning.

You should also ask a mundane question: what happens when you cannot come? A tutor with a clear answer has run a real teaching schedule before. A tutor who has never thought about it will leave gaps in February.

An IGCSE home tutor in Tardeo worth keeping will send a short note after each lesson naming what was covered and what went wrong, and will tell you when the real problem is not the subject. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rates, because neither can be honestly verified. The platform's job is to make sure the three people on your shortlist are who they say they are.

sections.heading: Which months of the Mumbai school year decide an IGCSE grade?
paragraphs: The decisive stretch is earlier than parents think. By the time mocks are returned, the content is taught and the remaining gains are technique. The months that actually decide the outcome are the ones in the middle of Year 10 and the start of Year 11, when new content is still arriving and a student who is quietly a topic behind can still catch up without sacrificing revision. Hiring an IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents found in the final weeks buys damage limitation, not a different grade.

Three pressure points recur. The first is the return from the long holidays, when schools compress a lot of teaching into a short run and any pre-existing gap widens fast. The second is the mock season, which in Tardeo arrives for a whole neighbourhood at once because one campus sets the local calendar. The third is the gap between mocks and the written series, which looks like plenty of time and disappears.

What a tutor does differs in each. Before the mocks, teach content and build method habits. During the mock aftermath, work the specific question types that failed, with the marked scripts open, rather than revising the whole syllabus again. In the final run, time papers under real conditions, because almost every student who knows the material and still underperforms is losing marks to pacing.

Fees track this calendar too. IGCSE tuition fees in Tardeo depend on the board, the tier, how scarce the subject specialist is, the lesson length and frequency, and the travel the tutor absorbs. Demand in the pre-examination months is high and good tutors are booked, so the family that arranges a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai households need in September pays for a calmer year than the one searching in January. We publish no price list, because a number quoted without knowing the subject and the tier would be a guess.

sections.heading: The four-week, one-term and one-series view of real progress
paragraphs: At four weeks, the honest measure is whether your child can tell you what a question is asking. That sounds modest. It is the whole game in IGCSE, where a large share of lost marks come from students answering a question adjacent to the one printed. Other early signals: working shown without being nagged, a graph labelled first time, homework started before Sunday evening. Marks at four weeks tell you almost nothing and should not be used to judge the match.

At one term, expect measurable technique gains. Fewer careless losses on the first page of a paper. A past-paper score that moves in the sections you worked on, even if the overall figure is flat because the untouched sections are now the weak ones. A coursework draft that was handed in on time. If none of that has happened in a full term of weekly lessons, the plan is wrong, and a competent tutor will say so before you do.

At one examination series, grades move or they do not, and both can happen alongside genuine improvement because the content got harder as the student got better. A student who was coasting on recall and is now being examined on application may hold the same grade while standing on much firmer ground. Judge the tutor on whether they can show you which question types still fail.

The limits are real. Tutoring will not undo a tier entry that was wrong, cannot substitute for school teaching, and does nothing for a student who does no work between lessons. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor promising a specific grade in a specific series is promising something nobody can deliver.
bullets: Week four: can the child state what the question is asking?

sections.heading: Booking IGCSE home classes in Tardeo, Mumbai: a practical checklist
paragraphs: Collect four things first. The board and the syllabus codes, which are printed on the school's subject list and save a week of guesswork. The most recent marked work, mock paper included, because the script shows a tutor the pattern of loss in minutes. Confirmation of tier entry where the subject has one. And two realistic evening windows, tested against the school bus timing and whatever else fills the week.

The first lesson should be diagnostic, and it should be slightly dull. A good tutor will not teach this week's chapter. They will hand your child a past question, watch how they start, stop them at the first wrong turn, and work backwards until they find where the reasoning actually broke. By the end you should have a short verdict and a plan covering the next four lessons, with a checkpoint named.

Settle logistics in the first week too: the fixed slot, the room, the visitor and gate arrangement at your building, who to tell when a lesson has to move, and the format of the tutor's weekly note. Tutoring in Mumbai fails on logistics more often than on teaching, and logistics are the easy part to fix in advance.

One more piece of preparation pays for itself: decide what you will stop doing. Most Year 10 households in Tardeo are already full. If a tutor is coming twice a week, something else in the week has to move, and the thing that usually gets sacrificed by accident is sleep. Choose the sacrifice deliberately instead, because a tired student learns nothing from an excellent tutor.
If the match is wrong, say it early. Changing a tutor in October costs a fortnight of momentum. Changing one in February costs the preparation that actually counted.
bullets: Bring board, syllabus codes, tier entry and the latest marked paper
Expect a diagnostic first lesson that goes backwards, not forwards
Ask for a named four-lesson plan with a checkpoint at the end
Fix slot, room, gate access and the missed-lesson rule in week one
Flag a poor match in the first month, not in the final term

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Tardeo cover in the first four lessons?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis first, then the two or three weaknesses costing the most marks. Lesson one uses a past question to find where your child's reasoning breaks rather than teaching the current chapter. Lessons two to four work that gap directly, with technique built in: showing method, reading command words, labelling graphs. There should be a checkpoint at the end of the month, usually a short timed section, so you can see whether the plan is working. A tutor who starts by covering this week's school topic is following the timetable rather than your child.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our Tardeo building for an evening slot on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is exactly why we match inside the island. A tutor already teaching on Cumballa Hill, Peddar Road or Mahalaxmi can hold a Tardeo evening slot for two years because the journey is short and the same every week. One coming from the suburbs through the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at that hour will eventually start cancelling, and cancellations in the mock term do real damage. Give two windows when you enquire, and mention lift or gate delays so the tutor plans for them.

faqs.question: How do we handle society gate passes and visitor entry for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once rather than signing them in every week. Most buildings around Tardeo and Cumballa Hill want resident authorisation for a visitor, and many will issue a standing arrangement for a fixed weekly slot if you ask the security desk directly. Provide the tutor's name, a photograph and the regular day and time. Experienced South Mumbai tutors expect this. The only thing that reliably causes a problem at the gate is an unannounced substitute, so tell the desk the day before if anything changes.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core. Can a tutor move them to Extended?
faqs.answer: No tutor can change an entry; the school does that, and there is a deadline. What a tutor can do is produce evidence. If your child is handling Extended-level questions in lessons, ask the tutor to set a full Extended past paper under timed conditions and send you the marked script. That script, taken to the subject teacher or the IGCSE coordinator early in the year, is a far stronger case than a parent's opinion. Leave it until the entry window has closed and the conversation is academic in the unhelpful sense.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Tardeo actually depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and tier, subject scarcity, lesson length and frequency, and travel. A tutor who has taught the Extended papers for a specific board and can mark to the specification sits at the top of the range; a generalist covering Year 9 basics sits well below. Travel is a real cost on the island because an evening journey eats a tutor's time whatever the distance. We publish no figures, because a rate quoted without knowing the subject, the tier and the address would mislead you. Ask what the rate includes and whether it changes before examinations.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for IGCSE coursework and practical components?
faqs.answer: It works well for coursework and poorly for practical technique. Coursework is a document, so a tutor reading a draft on a shared screen and asking why a paragraph exists is doing exactly the right job. Practical skills, including the habits the alternative-to-practical paper tests, are easier to build with someone beside the student watching them set up a table of results and omit the control. For most Year 10 and 11 students the sensible shape is home lessons for teaching and short online sessions for draft work.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge harder than Pearson Edexcel, or the other way round?
faqs.answer: Neither, and comparing them is the wrong question. They are different specifications with different paper structures, different coursework availability and different subject options, and your child is entered for one of them by their school. What matters is whether the tutor has taught that board's papers and can mark to its scheme. A tutor who is strong on Cambridge Physics and has never seen an Edexcel paper will still teach the content well and will misjudge what the examiner rewards. Ask which board they last taught to examination.

faqs.question: There has been no improvement after a month of lessons. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor three questions before changing anything. What have you worked on? What does my child still get wrong, specifically? What are you changing next month? A tutor with a real plan answers in detail and can show you work. If the diagnosis has not moved since lesson one, the match is wrong, and we will arrange a replacement without you starting the search again. A month is long enough to judge and early enough that switching costs you a fortnight rather than a term.

faqs.question: Do you cover Peddar Road, Mahalaxmi and Cumballa Hill from Tardeo?
faqs.answer: Yes. Those three plus the Tardeo-Jaslok corridor are the standard match radius, and many tutors teach in two of them in the same week. For addresses further across the island we look at the actual evening journey rather than claiming coverage, because a tutor who cannot reliably arrive is worse than a shorter shortlist. Nearest stations are Mumbai Central and Grant Road on the Western Line, which matters for tutors travelling by train. Send the address with your first message, not after the introduction.

faqs.question: Should a parent stay in the room during home tuition?
faqs.answer: Be in the flat, not in the room. For the first two or three lessons, being nearby helps you judge whether the tutor teaches or performs. After that, a parent in the room usually makes a Year 10 student less willing to admit confusion, which is the opposite of what you want. Keep the working space out of the bedroom if the flat allows it, keep the door open, and rely on the tutor's end-of-lesson note instead of listening in. If the note is vague for two weeks running, ask about it.

faqs.answer: As a search phrase, not as a verdict. Parents type best IGCSE tutor in Tardeo or IGCSE tutors near me Tardeo and get directories ranking tutors nobody at those sites has met. There is no ranking of tutors in this city that means anything. The useful questions are narrow: has this person taught my child's board and tier to examination, are they free when my child is home, and can they reach my building every week in July. A trial lesson answers more than any list.

sections.heading: Should a Year 9 student in Thane West take Core or Extended?
paragraphs: Enter for Extended unless there is a specific reason not to. The Core tier limits the grade available in Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics and in the tiered sciences, and that limit follows a child into Diploma Programme (DP) or A Level applications two years later. Most students at the IGCSE schools around Thane station are entered for Extended, and the ones who find it hard are usually struggling with pace, not with ceiling. Pace is what home tuition in this part of Mumbai is genuinely good at fixing.

IGCSE Years 9-11 is not three equal years. Year 9 is foundation work in most schools here, often taught on the school's own scheme rather than strictly to the syllabus, which is why a Year 9 report can look fine and a Year 10 report can fall off a cliff. Year 10 is where the examined content starts arriving at volume, and Year 11 is almost entirely consolidation, coursework and past papers. Grade scales and tier rules differ between Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel subjects, and between subjects within one board, so the school coordinator and the current syllabus document are the only reliable source for your child's specific entry. Do not take a figure from a tuition website, including this one.

Subject choice across both boards is the decision parents underestimate. A Year 9 picking options is choosing which doors stay open at 16, and the combination matters more than any single subject: dropping a science narrows DP options, dropping a second language narrows some university routes abroad, and taking three sciences plus Additional Mathematics makes Year 11 heavy in a way nobody warns you about in Year 9. Households that want all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Thane West tutors can cover between them usually end up with two names rather than one. There is no single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families take at once, and anyone who offers to be one is overselling.
